items.title: A uniformizer differential generates the module of differentials
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as required by thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free. Let k be a field, C a smooth integral curve over k, p a closed point with residue field kappa(p) finite separable over k, and t a uniformizer of O_{C,p}. Then: (1) Omega^1_{C/k,p} is a free rank-one O_{C,p}-module (thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free); (2) lem-ag-separable-residue-cotangent-sequence identifies m_p/m_p^2 with Omega^1_{C/k,p} tensor kappa(p), by the map sending the class of x to dx tensor 1. Since O_{C,p} is a DVR, the class of t is a basis of m_p/m_p^2, so dt reduces to a basis of the cotangent space; Nakayama then shows dt is a basis of Omega^1_{C/k,p}; (3) localizing at the generic point gives dt as a basis of Omega^1_{k(C)/k}, and every rational differential has a unique expression omega = a dt with a in k(C); (4) completion preserves this basis. In particular, when k is perfect the result applies at every closed point.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)

items.strategy: Let A = O_{C,p}, m = (t), and kappa = kappa(p). By thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free, Omega^1_{A/k} is free of rank one. Since kappa/k is finite separable, lem-ag-separable-residue-cotangent-sequence makes m/m^2 -> Omega^1_{A/k} tensor_A kappa an isomorphism, with [t] mapping to dt tensor 1. The DVR supplier gives m=(t), so [t] is a basis of m/m^2. Thus dt has nonzero image in the cotangent space and Nakayama shows it generates the rank-one free stalk; in a free rank-one module a generator is a basis. Localizing this basis to the generic point gives a basis of Omega^1_{k(C)/k}, consistent with thm-ag-field-differentials-separable-rank, and completing the stalk preserves the basis. The perfect-field case follows because every algebraic residue extension of a perfect field is separable. This argument proves dt is a basis from its nonzero cotangent class; nonzero elements of a rank-one free module need not themselves be bases.

items.title: Residue of a rational differential at a separable closed point
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the differential and power-series suppliers. Let k be a field, C a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over k, and p a closed point with residue field kappa(p) finite separable over k. The completion of O_{C,p} has a unique k-compatible coefficient field kappa(p) -> Ohat_{C,p}; for any uniformizer t this identifies Ohat_{C,p} with kappa(p)[[t]]. For omega in Omega^1_{k(C)/k}, write omega = a dt uniquely by lem-uniformizer-differential-is-a-basis and expand a = sum_n a_n t^n in kappa(p)((t)). Define res_p(omega) := Tr_{kappa(p)/k}(a_{-1}), using def-field-norm-and-trace. The value is independent of t by lem-residue-independent-uniformizer, so the formula is well defined at every closed point with separable residue field. In particular it is defined at every closed point when k is perfect; no coefficient-trace formula is asserted at an inseparable closed point over an imperfect field.

references.title: MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25
Joseph Lipman, Residues, duality, and the fundamental class of a scheme-map (2011)
John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159

items.strategy: For the k-compatible coefficient field, choose a primitive element alpha for the finite separable extension kappa(p)/k and let P in k[X] be its monic minimal polynomial. Separability gives P'(alpha) != 0. The Noetherian local completion theorem and completion-preserves-regularity theorem show that Ohat_{C,p} is a complete Noetherian regular local domain of dimension one with residue field kappa(p); it is complete and separated. Hence it is Henselian by cor-complete-separated-adic-pair-henselian, and cor-factor-hensel-implies-simple-root-hensel lifts the simple residue root alpha of P uniquely to a root in Ohat_{C,p}. The resulting k-algebra map kappa(p)=k[alpha] -> Ohat_{C,p} is a section of the residue map; uniqueness of the root makes this section unique. For a uniformizer t, the parameter power-series map kappa(p)[[T]] -> Ohat_{C,p}, T |-> t, is injective by lem-parameter-power-series-map-injective-by-dimension and makes Ohat_{C,p} finite over its image by lem-parameter-power-series-subring-makes-ring-finite. Since Ohat_{C,p}/tOhat_{C,p}=kappa(p), complete Nakayama shows that the image generates Ohat_{C,p}; hence this map is surjective and identifies the completion with kappa(p)[[t]]. Now use the basis lemma to write omega=a dt uniquely and extract a_{-1}; finite separability makes the field trace a k-linear map to k. The uniformizer-independence lemma proves that the value does not depend on t. If k is perfect, cor-algebraic-extensions-of-perfect-fields-are-separable covers every closed point.

items.title: The residue is independent of the uniformizer
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the completion and
power-series suppliers. Let $k$ be a field, let $C$ be a smooth integral curve
over $k$, and let $p$ be a closed point whose residue field $\kappa(p)$ is
finite separable over $k$. Use the $k$-compatible coefficient field
$\kappa(p)\hookrightarrow\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,p}$ of
[[def-residue-rational-differential-curve-point]], and let $t$ and $t'$ be
uniformizers of $\mathcal O_{C,p}$. Write $t'=\theta(t)=t\,u(t)$ with
$u(t)$ a unit of $\kappa(p)[\![t]\!]$. For a rational differential $\omega$ write
$$\omega=a\,\mathrm dt=a'\,\mathrm dt',\qquad a,a'\in k(C),$$
using [[lem-uniformizer-differential-is-a-basis]], and expand $a$ in
$\kappa(p)((t))$ and $a'$ in $\kappa(p)((t'))$. Then
$$[t^{-1}]\,a=[t'^{-1}]\,a',$$
so the coefficient traces agree,
$\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(p)/k}([t^{-1}]a)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(p)/k}([t'^{-1}]a')$,
and the residue $\operatorname{res}_p(\omega)$ of
[[def-residue-rational-differential-curve-point]] does not depend on the
choice of uniformizer. The formal change-of-parameter identity holds in every
characteristic.

references.title: MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25
John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159
Joseph Lipman, Residues, duality, and the fundamental class of a scheme-map (2011)

items.strategy: Assume inherited Choice and finite separable residue field. Use the universal-property map Delta_t for algebraic differentials to derive j_t(a)=psi(theta(t))theta′(t) for the actual local uniformizers t,t′. For exponents n>=0 and n=-1, compute the t^{-1} coefficient directly. For n<=-2, express the coefficient as a Laurent polynomial over Z in finitely many unit-series coefficients; prove it zero in a universal characteristic-zero rational-function field by the formal substitution-residue identity, use injectivity into that field, and specialize the integral identity to every field. Finite negative tails give the coefficient identity; the trace preserves it. Formal series in the converse of F2 are uniformizers of the completed DVR only.

items.title: Residues of exact differentials vanish
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the completion and
coefficient-field/residue suppliers. Let $k$ be a field, $C$ a smooth integral
curve over $k$, and $p$ a closed point whose residue field $\kappa(p)$ is finite
separable over $k$. For every
$f\in k(C)$, the exact differential $\mathrm df$ has residue zero at $p$:
$$\operatorname{res}_p(\mathrm df)=0.$$
Consequently the residue functional kills the image of
$\mathrm d\colon k(C)\to\Omega^1_{k(C)/k}$, and adding an exact differential
does not change the residue at any point where the coefficient-trace residue
is defined. This holds in every characteristic.

references.title: MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25
John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159
Joseph Lipman, Residues, duality, and the fundamental class of a scheme-map (2011)

items.strategy: With the inherited Choice premise and finite separable residue field, embed K=k(C) into kappa(p)((t)) and write df=a dt. Type D composed with the completion embedding as a k-derivation K -> kappa(p)((t)); the universal property of algebraic Kähler differentials gives Delta_t with Delta_t(df)=D(j_t(f)) and Delta_t(dt)=1, so j_t(a)=D(j_t(f)). In the formal derivative, only n=0 can contribute to t^{-1}, and its coefficient is zero. The coefficient trace therefore vanishes. The argument uses no division by integers and applies in every characteristic.

items.title: The trace of a finite potent endomorphism exists and is unique
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the linear algebra suppliers. Let k be a field and V a k-vector space, and let theta be a k-linear endomorphism of V. Call theta finite potent when theta^n(V) is finite-dimensional for some n >= 0. Then there is a unique element Tr_V(theta) in k with the following three properties: (T1) if V is finite-dimensional, Tr_V(theta) is the ordinary trace of theta; (T2) if W is a theta-stable subspace of V, then Tr_V(theta) = Tr_W(theta) + Tr_{V/W}(theta); and (T3) if theta is nilpotent, then Tr_V(theta) = 0. Existence is by choosing n with W := theta^n(V) finite-dimensional and theta-stable and setting Tr_V(theta) := Tr_W(theta); the value is independent of n and of W, and any finite-dimensional theta-stable W containing theta^m(V) for some m computes it. In particular Tr_V is unchanged when V is replaced by any such W.

references.title: John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159

items.strategy: For existence take n with W = theta^n V finite-dimensional; W is theta-stable and the induced map on V/W is nilpotent, so by (T1) and (T3) the unique candidate is the ordinary trace of theta on W. Independence of n: if m >= n the map theta^{m-n} carries theta^nV onto theta^mV, and the trace of theta on theta^nV equals the trace of theta on the image plus the trace on the kernel, which is finite-dimensional and nilpotent for the induced map, so the two ordinary traces agree; this is the standard 'trace on a finite-dimensional quotient' computation. Uniqueness: (T2) applied to a theta-stable finite-dimensional W with theta^nV contained in W reduces the value to the ordinary trace on W, so the three properties determine Tr_V. No finite-dimensionality of V is assumed, only finite potency, and the only choice made is a basis of the auxiliary finite-dimensional space.

items.title: Commensurable subspaces and the ideal filtration E_0, E_1, E_2 of End_k(V)
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the linear algebra suppliers (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $k$ be a field, let $V$ be a $k$-vector space (def-vector-space), and let $A,B$ be $k$-subspaces of $V$. **Commensurability.** Write $A<B$, and say that $A$ is **not much bigger** than $B$, when the quotient $(A+B)/B$ (def-quotient-vector-space-and-canonical-projection) is finite-dimensional (def-dimension). Write $A\sim B$, and say that $A$ and $B$ are **commensurable**, when $A<B$ and $B<A$. Thus $A<B$ says that $A$ is contained in $B$ up to a finite-dimensional error: equivalently, and this reformulation is used throughout, $A<B$ holds if and only if $A\subseteq B+W$ for some finite-dimensional subspace $W\subseteq V$. The relation $<$ has the following elementary properties, each an immediate consequence of the definition; here $A$, $B$, $C$ are $k$-subspaces of $V$ and $r\ge0$. 1. *Reflexivity and monotonicity.* $A<A$ and $A<A+B$; if $A\subseteq B$ then $A<B$; if $A<B$ and $B\subseteq C$ then $A<C$; and $A<B$ if and only if $A<A\cap B$, if and only if $A+B<B$. 2. *Transitivity.* If $A<B$ and $B<C$, then $A<C$. 3. *$k$-linear maps.* If $A<B$ and $\theta\colon V\to V'$ is $k$-linear, then $\theta(A)<\theta(B)$ in $V'$ (def-linear-map). 4. *Finite sums.* If $A_i<B_i$ for $i=1,\dots,r$, then $\sum_i A_i<\sum_i B_i$. 5. *Commensurability is an equivalence relation.* The relation $\sim$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, and $A\sim B$ if and only if both $(A+B)/B$ and $(A+B)/A$ are finite-dimensional. For instance, $A<A$ because $(A+A)/A$ is the zero space; if $B\subseteq C$, then $(A+C)/C\cong A/(A\cap C)$ is a quotient of $(A+B)/B\cong A/(A\cap B)$. For transitivity, if $A<B$ and $B<C$, choose finite-dimensional subspaces $U,W\subseteq V$ with $A\subseteq B+U$ and $B\subseteq C+W$. Then $A\subseteq B+U\subseteq C+W+U$, so $A<C$. A $k$-linear $\theta$ induces a surjection $(A+B)/B\twoheadrightarrow\theta(A+B)/\theta(B)$, which proves 3. The reformulation $A<B\Leftrightarrow A\subseteq B+W$ for a finite-dimensional $W$ is obtained by lifting a finite spanning set of $(A+B)/B$ to $A$: every class has a representative in $A$, since each $A+B$ element differs from an element of $A$ by an element of $B$; the span of representatives of a finite basis is such a $W$. Conversely, if $A\subseteq B+W$ for finite-dimensional $W$, then $(A+B)/B$ is a quotient of the image of $W$ and is finite-dimensional. Now let $K$ be a commutative $k$-algebra acting on $V$ (equivalently, $V$ is a $K$-module whose structure map is $k$-linear) and assume $$fA<A\qquad\text{for every }f\in K.$$ Attached to the pair $(V,A)$ is the **ideal filtration** $$E:=\{\theta\in\operatorname{End}_k(V):\theta A<A\},\qquad E_1:=\{\theta\in\operatorname{End}_k(V):\theta V<A\},\qquad E_2:=\{\theta\in\operatorname{End}_k(V):\theta A<0\},\qquad E_0:=E_1\cap E_2,$$ where $\theta A<0$ is shorthand for the statement that $\theta A$ is finite-dimensional, the zero space $0$ being finite-dimensional. Thus $$E_0=\{\theta\in\operatorname{End}_k(V):\theta V<A\text{ and }\theta A\text{ is finite-dimensional}\}.$$ Properties 1 and 4 show that $E$, $E_1$ and $E_2$ are closed under addition and under multiplication by scalars, hence are $k$-subspaces of $\operatorname{End}_k(V)$. The image of $K$ is contained in $E$ by the hypothesis $fA<A$ for every $f\in K$; it need not be contained in $E_1$ or $E_2$. Also $E_0=E_1\cap E_2$ by definition. An element of $E_0$ is *finite potent* in the sense of lem-finite-potent-trace-existence-and-uniqueness: if $\theta V<A$ with $\theta V\subseteq A+W$ for a finite-dimensional $W$, then $\theta^2V\subseteq\theta A+\theta W$, a sum of two finite-dimensional spaces, so $\theta^2V$ is finite-dimensional and the trace $\operatorname{Tr}_V(\theta)$ is defined. The subspaces $E$, $E_1$, $E_2$ depend only on the commensurability class of $A$: if $A'\sim A$ is a further $k$-subspace of $V$ with $fA'<A'$ for all $f\in K$, then properties 2 and 3 give $\theta A'<\theta A<A<A'$, and symmetrically, for every $\theta\in\operatorname{End}_k(V)$, so $E(A')=E(A)$, $E_1(A')=E_1(A)$ and $E_2(A')=E_2(A)$, and consequently $E_0(A')=E_0(A)$. These are the subspaces in which Tate's abstract residue theory states its residue map on $K\,dK$; they are abstract linear-algebraic objects and involve no geometry.

references.title: John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159

items.strategy: Translate the finite quotient (A+B)/B into a finite-dimensional error witness by lifting quotient basis classes to A. Prove relation properties using finite witnesses and quotient maps. Define E,E1,E2,E0; show K maps into E only and E0 elements are finite potent by the square-image bound.

items.title: Linearity and conjugation invariance of the finite potent trace
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the linear algebra suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field and $V$ a $k$-vector space ([[def-vector-space]]), and let $\operatorname{Tr}_V$ be the trace of finite potent endomorphisms supplied by [[lem-finite-potent-trace-existence-and-uniqueness]]. **(T4)** Let $F\subseteq\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ be a $k$-subspace that is *finite potent*, meaning that there is an integer $n\ge0$ such that $\theta_1\cdots\theta_n(V)$ is finite-dimensional ([[def-dimension]]) for every choice of elements $\theta_1,\dots,\theta_n\in F$. Then $\operatorname{Tr}_V$ restricted to $F$ is $k$-linear ([[def-linear-map]]). **(T5)** If $\varphi\colon V'\to V$ and $\psi\colon V\to V'$ are $k$-linear and $\psi\varphi$ is finite potent, then $\varphi\psi$ is finite potent and $$\operatorname{Tr}_V(\varphi\psi)=\operatorname{Tr}_{V'}(\psi\varphi).$$ **(T6)** Let $A\subseteq V$ be a $k$-subspace and let $E,E_1,E_2,E_0$ be the subspaces of $\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ attached to $A$ in [[def-commensurable-subspaces-and-ideals-of-endomorphisms]]. - **(a)** If $\theta\colon V\to V$ has finite-dimensional image, then for every $k$-linear $\sigma\colon V\to V$ the commutator $[\theta,\sigma]=\theta\sigma-\sigma\theta$ is finite potent and $\operatorname{Tr}_V([\theta,\sigma])=0$. - **(b)** If $\gamma\in E_0$ and $\psi\in E$, or if $\gamma\in E_1$ and $\psi\in E_2$, then $[\gamma,\psi]\in E_0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_V([\gamma,\psi])=0$.

references.title: John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159

items.title: E is a k-algebra, the E_i are ideals, and commutator traces vanish
items.statement: Keep the notation of def-commensurable-subspaces-and-ideals-of-endomorphisms: $k$ is a field, $V$ a $k$-vector space (def-vector-space), $A\subseteq V$ a $k$-subspace, $K$ a commutative $k$-algebra acting on $V$ with $fA<A$ for all $f\in K$, and $E,E_1,E_2,E_0$ are the $k$-subspaces of $\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ attached to $A$. Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the linear algebra suppliers (def-axiom-of-choice). Then: 1. $E$ is a $k$-subalgebra of $\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ containing the image of $K$, and $E_1,E_2$ are two-sided ideals of $E$; 2. $E_1+E_2=E$ and $E_1\cap E_2=E_0$; 3. $E_0$ is a finite potent subspace of $\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ in the sense of lem-finite-potent-trace-linearity-and-conjugation, so the trace $\operatorname{Tr}_V$ of lem-finite-potent-trace-existence-and-uniqueness is defined on $E_0$ and is $k$-linear there (def-linear-map); 4. if $\gamma\in E_0$ and $\psi\in E$, or if $\gamma\in E_1$ and $\psi\in E_2$, then the commutator $[\gamma,\psi]=\gamma\psi-\psi\gamma$ lies in $E_0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_V([\gamma,\psi])=0$.

references.title: John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the abstract residue map res_V: Omega^1_{K/k} -> k
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the linear algebra suppliers (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $k$ be a field, $K$ a commutative $k$-algebra (def-vector-space, def-linear-map), $V$ a $K$-module, and $A\subseteq V$ a $k$-subspace with $fA<A$ for every $f\in K$, in the sense of def-commensurable-subspaces-and-ideals-of-endomorphisms, so that the subspaces $E,E_1,E_2,E_0$ of $\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ are defined. Then there is a unique $k$-linear map $$\operatorname{res}_V\colon\Omega^1_{K/k}\longrightarrow k$$ (def-kahler-differentials-algebra, cor-derivations-represented-by-differentials) such that $$\operatorname{res}_V(f\,\mathrm{d}g)=\operatorname{Tr}_V([f_1,g_1])$$ for all $f,g\in K$ and all endomorphisms $f_1,g_1\in E$ satisfying $f_1\equiv f\pmod{E_2}$, $g_1\equiv g\pmod{E_2}$ and with $f_1\in E_1$ or $g_1\in E_1$. Here $\operatorname{Tr}_V$ is the finite potent trace of lem-finite-potent-trace-linearity-and-conjugation and $[f_1,g_1]=f_1g_1-g_1f_1$. Existence uses that $E=E_1+E_2$, so such lifts always exist; the value is independent of the lifts by lem-e-ideals-and-commutator-trace, and $k$-bilinear in $(f,g)$ by the linearity of the trace on the finite potent subspace $E_0$. The map is denoted $\operatorname{res}_V$, or $\operatorname{res}_A$, and is the abstract residue attached to the pair $(V,A)$.

references.title: John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159

items.strategy: Lift both arguments into E1, define the commutator trace, and prove lift independence with the E1/E2 commutator supplier. Its bilinear Leibniz form descends through an explicit K-module on the tensor-symbol quotient, which is identified with Ω¹_{K/k} via the universal derivation and inverse maps on generators.

items.title: Basic properties of the abstract residue: restriction, commensurability, vanishing, logarithmic residues
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the linear algebra suppliers (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $k$ be a field, $K$ a commutative $k$-algebra (def-linear-map), $V$ a $K$-module and $A\subseteq V$ a $k$-subspace with $fA<A$ for every $f\in K$ in the sense of def-commensurable-subspaces-and-ideals-of-endomorphisms, so that the abstract residue $\operatorname{res}_V$ of thm-abstract-residue-exists-unique is defined. **(1) (Restriction and commensurability.)** If $A\subseteq V'\subseteq V$ is a $k$-subspace with $KV'\subseteq V'$, then $\operatorname{res}_V=\operatorname{res}_{V'}$ as $k$-linear maps on $\Omega^1_{K/k}$; if $A'\sim A$ is a further $k$-subspace of $V$ with $fA'<A'$ for all $f\in K$, then $\operatorname{res}_{A'}=\operatorname{res}_A$; and if $V/A$ is finite-dimensional then $\operatorname{res}_V=0$. **(2) (Continuity.)** If $$fA+fgA+fg^2A\subseteq A,$$ then $\operatorname{res}_V(f\,\mathrm dg)=0$. In particular, this holds when $fA\subseteq A$ and $gA\subseteq A$ — equivalently, when $fA+gA+fgA\subseteq A$. Thus $\operatorname{res}_V$ is identically zero when $A$ is a $K$-submodule of $V$. **(3) (Logarithmic and power residues.)** $\operatorname{res}_V(f^n\,\mathrm df)=0$ for every $f\in K$ and every integer $n\ge0$, and also for every integer $n\le-2$ when $f$ is invertible in $K$; in particular $\operatorname{res}_V(\mathrm df)=0$ for every $f\in K$. **(4) (Logarithmic residues along a unit.)** Let $g\in K^\times$ and let $h\in K$ with $hA\subseteq A$. Then $hgA=ghA\subseteq gA$, so multiplication by $h$ induces $k$-linear endomorphisms $m_h$ of the finite-dimensional spaces $A/(A\cap gA)$ and $gA/(A\cap gA)$ (def-dimension, def-trace-of-an-endomorphism), and $$\operatorname{res}_V(hg^{-1}\,\mathrm dg)=\operatorname{Tr}_{A/(A\cap gA)}(m_h)-\operatorname{Tr}_{gA/(A\cap gA)}(m_h).$$ In particular, if $gA\subseteq A$ then $A\cap gA=gA$ and taking $h=1$ gives $\operatorname{res}_V(g^{-1}\mathrm dg)=\dim_k(A/gA)$.

references.title: John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159

Prove the full Tate condition fA+fgA+fg²A⊂A makes [πf,g] square-zero. Derive power residues and the logarithmic quotient formula by preserving A∩gA and computing on (A+gA)/(A∩gA).

items.title: Additivity of the abstract residue over intersecting subspaces
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the linear algebra suppliers. Let $k$, $K$, $V$ and $A$ be as in thm-abstract-residue-exists-unique, and let $B$ be a further $k$-subspace of $V$ with $fB<B$ for every $f\in K$. Then $A+B$ and $A\cap B$ are also stable in the sense that $f(A+B)<A+B$ and $f(A\cap B)<A\cap B$ for all $f\in K$, and $$\operatorname{res}_{A+B}+\operatorname{res}_{A\cap B} =\operatorname{res}_A+\operatorname{res}_B$$ as $k$-linear maps $\Omega^1_{K/k}\to k$. This is the additivity formula $(R_5)$ that turns the local residue at a finite set of points into a sum of local residues and drives the global residue theorem.

references.title: John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159

items.strategy: Establish stability of A+B and A∩B. Choose compatible complements so π_A+π_B=π_{A+B}+π_{A∩B}, express each residue as Tr([π_C f,g]), and compare the two equal commutator differences. Prove T4 applies to the two spans of pairs of traces by explicit finite-potence filtrations (length 3 for A⊂A+B and length 4 for A∩B⊂B⊂A+B).

items.title: The abstract residue under a finite free extension of the coefficient algebra
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the linear algebra suppliers. Let $K'$ be a commutative $K$-algebra which is a free $K$-module of finite rank, with a $K$-basis $x_1,\dots,x_n$, let $V$ be a $K$-module and $A$ a $k$-subspace with $fA<A$ for every $f\in K$, and let $V':=K'\otimes_KV$, $A':=\sum_i x_i\otimes A$. Then $K'$ acts on $V'$ with $f'A'<A'$ for every $f'\in K'$, the commensurability class of $A'$ is independent of the chosen $K$-basis, and for every $f\in K'$ and $g\in K$ one has $$\operatorname{res}^{V'}(f\,\mathrm dg) =\operatorname{res}^{V}(\operatorname{Tr}_{K'/K}(f)\,\mathrm dg),$$ where $\operatorname{Tr}_{K'/K}$ is the trace of multiplication on the free $K$-module $K'$. This is $(R_6)$ of Tate's paper.

items.title: The abstract residue computes the coefficient-trace residue at every closed point
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the residue suppliers. Let $C$ be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a perfect field $k$ and let $p$ be a closed point with residue field $\kappa(p)$, uniformizer $t$ and a fixed coefficient field $\kappa(p)\hookrightarrow\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,p}$ identifying $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,p}$ with $\kappa(p)[\![t]\!]$. (1) If $\kappa(p)=k$, so that $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,p}=k[\![t]\!]$, and $f=\sum_na_nt^n$, $g=\sum_mb_mt^m$ are elements of $k((t))$, then the abstract residue of lem-abstract-residue-basic-properties satisfies $$\operatorname{res}_p(f\,\mathrm dg) =\ \text{coefficient of }t^{-1}\text{ in }f(t)g'(t) =\sum_{n+m=0}ma_nb_m,$$ where $g'$ is the formal derivative of $g$. (2) For an arbitrary closed point $p$ of $C$ and $\omega=f\,\mathrm dt$ with $f\in k(C)$ expanded as $\sum_na_nt^n$ in $\kappa(p)((t))$, the abstract residue equals the coefficient-trace residue of def-residue-rational-differential-curve-point: $$\operatorname{res}_p(\omega)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\kappa(p)/k}(a_{-1}).$$ In particular the two residue definitions used on this page agree at every closed point of $C$, and the global residue theorem may be stated for either of them.

For general series truncate both variables and prove tails vanish by continuity and order bounds; then apply the finite-free extension formula using a fixed k-basis of κ(p) to obtain coefficientwise field trace.

items.title: The adele quotient V_X/(K + A_X) computes H^1 of the structure sheaf
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the coherent-cohomology suppliers. Let X be a connected regular curve of dimension one, proper over the field k, with function field K = k(X) and closed points p. Put V_X := { (f_p) in the product of the completions K_p of K at the closed points : f_p lies in the valuation ring A_p for all but finitely many p }, A_X := the product of the rings A_p, and embed K diagonally. Then K is a k-subspace of V_X, one has f A_X < A_X and f A_X + f g A_X + f g^{-1} A_X contained in A_X + K for all f, g in K, the intersection K intersected with A_X is the space of global sections H^0(X, O_X), and there is a canonical k-linear isomorphism V_X/(K + A_X) isomorphic to H^1(X, O_X). In particular V_X/(K + A_X) is finite-dimensional, and for a geometrically integral X one has K intersected with A_X = k.

items.strategy: Consider the sheaves K^0 and K^1 on X given on an open U by K^0(U) = image of K in the product of the K_p for p in U and K^1(U) = that product modulo the product of the A_p; restriction maps of K^1 are surjective, so K^1 has no higher cohomology (thm-flasque-sheaves-acyclic, applied after the constant-sheaf identification of the diagonal image), while K^0 is the constant sheaf with value K and is flasque on the irreducible space X. The adjunction-style sequence 0 -> O_X -> K^0 -> K^1 -> 0 is exact in the middle: on an affine chart U = Spec A the ring A is a one-dimensional domain with fraction field K (def-zero-divisor-and-integral-domain, def-field-of-fractions, lem-integral-finite-type-scheme-function-field), the closed points of U are exactly the maximal ideals of A (cor-closed-points-of-spectrum-are-maximal-ideals) and the stalk of O_X at a closed point p is the localisation A_p inside K (thm-stalk-structure-sheaf-prime-localization, def-localisation-at-a-prime-ideal), so the kernel of K -> product over the closed p in U of K_p/A_p is the set of f in K lying in A_p for every maximal ideal p; such an f lies in A, because otherwise the ideal of denominators I(f) = {a in A : af in A} is proper and hence contained in a maximal ideal m (thm-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal-ideal, thm-field-of-fractions-is-a-field-and-the-domain-embeds), while f = s/t with s in A and t not in m would force t in I(f) contained in m, a contradiction, so f is not in A_m; conversely A lies in every A_p. Exactness on an affine cover gives exactness of the sequence of sheaves, and its global sections compute, by the long exact sequence (cor-derived-long-exact-sequence) and the vanishing of the higher cohomology of K^0 and K^1, a canonical isomorphism V_X/(K + A_X) = coker(K -> V_X/A_X) isomorphic to H^1(X, O_X) and an identification of the kernel with H^0(X, O_X) = K intersected with A_X. This is the well-known presentation of H^1 of a curve by adeles, quoted by Tate as the last step of his proof of Theorem 3; finite dimensionality follows from the finiteness of coherent cohomology on a proper curve. For X geometrically integral and proper, H^0(X, O_X) = k by the structure-sheaf theorem.

items.title: The global residue theorem on a smooth proper curve over a perfect field
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the residue and coherent-cohomology suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a perfect field k and let omega be a rational differential on C. Then res_p(omega) is nonzero at only finitely many closed points p of C, and the sum of the residues vanishes: sum over all closed points p of C of res_p(omega) = 0. The residue may be computed by the coefficient-trace formula of def-residue-rational-differential-curve-point (agreement is cor-coefficient-trace-residue-agreement); the statement is characteristic-free and no separability hypothesis beyond perfectness of k is used.

For the finite pole block and restricted-product tail prove hA<A for every h using finite local quotient dimensions. Construct admissible block lifts, prove their block commutator finite potent with a common exponent, and split its trace using T2. At regular points uniformizer differentials form a local basis. Verify the full R2 condition fA+fgA+fg^2A⊂A on the integral tail. Local coefficient-trace agreement yields finite support and sum zero.

items.title: Principal parts of an invertible sheaf on a curve
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the curve and sheaf suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]); AC implies Dependent Choice by
[[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], which supplies the
choice hypothesis of the finite-support lemma below. Let $k$ be a field and
let $C$ be a smooth proper
geometrically integral curve over $k$ ([[def-algebraic-curve-over-field]]),
with generic point $\eta$ ([[def-generic-point-irreducible-closed-subset]]) and
function field $K=\mathcal O_{C,\eta}=k(C)$
([[lem-integral-finite-type-scheme-function-field]]). Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible
$\mathcal O_C$-module ([[def-invertible-sheaf]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]).

**Sheaf of rational sections.** The sheaf $\mathcal L_\eta$ of rational
sections of $\mathcal L$ is the constant sheaf with value the generic stalk
$\mathcal L_\eta$, a one-dimensional $K$-vector space
([[def-rational-section-line-bundle]],
[[lem-constant-sheaf-is-the-sheaf-of-locally-constant-functions]],
[[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]]); a **rational section** is a global
section of this sheaf, equivalently an element of $\mathcal L_\eta$. The
natural map $\mathcal L\to\mathcal L_\eta$ is injective: on an affine
trivializing open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ it is the map $A\to K$ in a
frame, and $A$ is a domain because $C$ is integral
([[def-invertible-sheaf]], [[def-algebraic-curve-over-field]]).

**Sheaf of principal parts.** Define
$$\mathcal P(\mathcal L):=\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal L\longrightarrow\mathcal L_\eta)=\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L.$$
The stalk sequence is exact by
[[thm-exactness-of-sheaves-stalkwise]]. At the generic point the two stalks
are both $\mathcal L_\eta$, so $\mathcal P(\mathcal L)_\eta=0$. At a
closed point $p$, exactness gives
$$\mathcal P(\mathcal L)_p=\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p.$$
Trivializing $\mathcal L_p=A_pe_{\mathcal L}$ identifies this quotient
with $K/A_p$, where $A_p=\mathcal O_{C,p}$ is a DVR with uniformizer
$t_p$ ([[thm-local-ring-smooth-curve-dvr]]). It is a torsion $A_p$-module:
if a class is represented by $a/b$ with $a,b\in A_p$ and $b\ne0$, then
multiplication by $b$ kills it. By the published DVR normal-form theorem
[[thm-dvr-element-normal-form]], every class belongs to some submodule
$t_p^{-n}A_p/A_p$ with $n\ge0$: if its representative has valuation $m<0$,
take $n=-m$; if $m\ge0$, its class is zero. Multiplication by $t_p^n$ identifies
that submodule with $A_p/(t_p^n)$, which has length $n$ by
[[thm-dvr-ideal-and-module-length]]. Thus $K/A_p$ is the union of these
finite-length torsion submodules. A **local principal part** at $p$ is an
element of $\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p$.

**Quasi-coherence.** On an affine trivializing open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$
with fraction field $K$, the restriction of $\mathcal L_\eta$ is the
associated sheaf $\widetilde K$: on a distinguished open $D(f)$ with
$f\ne0$, the constant sheaf has sections $K$ and
$\widetilde K(D(f))=K_f=K$; on $D(0)=\varnothing$ both have zero sections.
The restriction of $\mathcal L$ is $\widetilde A$. Therefore both are
quasi-coherent, and their quotient is quasi-coherent by the published
[[thm-kernels-cokernels-qc-modules]]. The principal-parts sheaf is torsion,
not coherent; its stalk $K/A_p$ is not finitely generated over the DVR.
([[def-associated-sheaf-module-affine-scheme]],
[[thm-sections-basic-open-affine-scheme]],
[[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]])

**Finite support of rational sections.** First verify the hypotheses of
[[lem-principal-weil-divisor-locally-finite]]. The affine coordinate rings of
$C$ are finite-type algebras over the Noetherian field $k$ ([[def-field]]), hence Noetherian
by [[cor-finite-type-algebra-over-noetherian-ring-is-noetherian]]; thus $C$ is
locally Noetherian. It is quasi-compact because its structure morphism is
proper ([[def-proper-morphism]]), so $C$ is Noetherian in the sense of
[[def-locally-noetherian-and-noetherian-scheme]]. Every point is either the
generic point or closed, since $C$ is integral of dimension one. The generic
local ring is the field $K$; every closed-point local ring is a DVR by
[[thm-local-ring-smooth-curve-dvr]]. A field is integrally closed; a DVR is a
valuation ring by [[def-discrete-valuation-ring]] and therefore integrally closed by
[[thm-valuation-ring-is-integrally-closed]]. Thus all local rings are
integrally closed domains, so $C$ is normal in the sense required by
[[def-weil-divisor-normal-noetherian-scheme]]. In particular, each closed
point is a prime divisor.

Now choose a finite affine cover by opens trivializing $\mathcal L$ for a
nonzero global rational section $s$. On each such open $U_i$, write
$s|_{U_i}=f_i e_i$ with $f_i\in K^\times$, viewed as a global section of the
constant sheaf of meromorphic functions $\mathcal K_C$
([[def-sheaf-total-quotient-rings]],
[[lem-constant-sheaf-is-the-sheaf-of-locally-constant-functions]]). Every closed point of the
smooth integral curve is a prime divisor. The support where
$\operatorname{ord}_p(f_i)\ne0$ is locally finite by
[[lem-principal-weil-divisor-locally-finite]], hence finite on $C$ by
quasi-compactness. Taking the finite union over the cover shows that $s$ is
regular at all but finitely many closed points; indeed, outside this union
each $f_i$ is a unit in the local DVR, so $s$ is a local generator. The zero
rational section is regular everywhere. This uses only the local coefficient
of a rational section and the stated principal-Weil-divisor supplier; it does
not require a Cartier-divisor identification.

**The direct sum of skyscrapers.** For each closed point $p$, let
$\mathcal S_p$ be the skyscraper sheaf with value
$\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p$ at $p$ and zero stalks elsewhere, with
$\mathcal O_C$ acting through $\mathcal O_{C,p}$ at $p$
([[def-skyscraper-sheaf-abelian-group]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]). Put
$$\mathcal S:=\bigoplus_{p\in C_{\mathrm{closed}}}\mathcal S_p.$$
By [[lem-stalks-and-colimits-of-the-abelian-sheaf-tensor-product]], this
coproduct is the sheafification of the presheaf direct sum and its stalk at
any point is the direct sum of the summand stalks. By the sheafification
property [[def-sheafification]], a section of this sheafification is locally
represented by finite-support families, so its
support is locally finite.

For any open $U$ and $q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal L)(U)$, the quotient map
locally lifts $q$ to a rational section $r$
([[def-kernel-cokernel-image-sheaves]], [[def-sheafification]]). Around each $x\in U$, shrink
to an affine trivializing neighborhood on which a lift exists and write
$r=f e$ (or $r=0$); here $f\in K$ gives a global rational coefficient, so
the preceding finite-support argument applies. The nonzero stalks of $q$
there are contained in the finite pole support of $r$. Hence
the family of germs $(q_p)_{p\in U\cap C_{\mathrm{closed}}}$ is locally
finite and defines a section of $\mathcal S(U)$. This assignment gives a
natural $\mathcal O_C$-linear sheaf morphism
$$\gamma:\mathcal P(\mathcal L)\longrightarrow\mathcal S.$$
At a closed point $p$, the stalk map is the identity on
$\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p$: the $p$-summand is the only summand with
nonzero stalk there. At the generic point both stalks vanish, since every
closed point has a neighborhood of $\eta$ avoiding it and coproduct stalks
are direct sums. Thus $\gamma$ is an isomorphism by the published
[[thm-sheaf-morphism-isomorphism-stalkwise]]. This proves that
$\mathcal P(\mathcal L)$ is the direct sum of the closed-point skyscraper
sheaves with the stated fibers.

Because $C$ is quasi-compact, a locally finite support subset of $C$ is
finite. Consequently
$$H^0(C,\mathcal P(\mathcal L))=\bigoplus_{p\in C_{\mathrm{closed}}}\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p$$
is the vector space of finite-support families of local principal parts.
For every global rational section $s\in\mathcal L_\eta$, its diagonal
family $(s+\mathcal L_p)_p$ has finite support by the preceding argument,
so the diagonal map
$$\mathcal L_\eta\longrightarrow H^0(C,\mathcal P(\mathcal L)),\qquad s\longmapsto(s+\mathcal L_p)_p$$
is well-defined. Its image consists of the principal parts of global
rational sections. A global regular section maps to zero because each of its
germs lies in $\mathcal L_p$. The quotient of finite-support principal
parts by this diagonal image is the cohomology space computed in the next
item of this development.

items.strategy: Define the rational-section sheaf and its quotient P(L)=L_eta/L. Check the generic and closed stalks; use the DVR normal form to prove torsion and identify the local finite-length submodules t^{-n}A_p/A_p. Prove quasi-coherence without claiming coherence. Establish normality and Noetherian hypotheses before applying the finite-support divisor lemma. Construct the morphism from P(L) to the direct sum of skyscraper sheaves and verify it is an isomorphism on every stalk. Quasi-compactness turns locally finite support into finite support and gives the diagonal principal-parts map. No Cartier-divisor identification is used.

items.title: H^1 of a line bundle on a curve as principal parts modulo meromorphic and regular sections
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the flasque-acyclicity
supplier. Let $k$ be a field, let $C$ be a smooth proper geometrically
integral curve over $k$, and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible
$\mathcal O_C$-module. Let $\mathcal L_\eta$ be the constant sheaf of meromorphic
sections of $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal P(\mathcal L)=\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L$
its sheaf of principal parts, with stalks
$\mathcal P(\mathcal L)_p=\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p$ at the closed points
$p$. Then there is a canonical $k$-linear isomorphism
$$H^1(C,\mathcal L)\;\cong\;\operatorname{coker}\Bigl(\mathcal L_\eta\longrightarrow\textstyle\bigoplus_p \mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p\Bigr),$$
that is, $H^1(C,\mathcal L)$ is the $k$-vector space of finite-support families
of local principal parts modulo the principal parts of global meromorphic
sections of $\mathcal L$. Equivalently, it is the cokernel of the map
$H^0(C,\mathcal L_\eta)\to H^0(C,\mathcal P(\mathcal L))$ induced by the short
exact sequence $0\to\mathcal L\to\mathcal L_\eta\to\mathcal P(\mathcal L)\to0$.
The classes of global meromorphic sections are the coboundaries. A global
regular section has zero principal part at every closed point, so a class is
represented by finitely many local principal parts modulo global meromorphic
principal parts.

items.strategy: Use 0 -> L -> L_eta -> P(L) -> 0 and verify exactness at the generic and closed stalks. The constant sheaf L_eta is flasque on irreducible C, hence acyclic; the long exact sequence identifies H^1(C,L) with the cokernel of L_eta -> H^0(C,P(L)). The principal-parts definition identifies H^0(C,P(L)) with finite-support local parts. A global regular germ maps componentwise to zero; no common global lift of an arbitrary family is claimed.

items.title: The residue pairing of a line bundle with the dual canonical twist
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the residue suppliers (def-axiom-of-choice). Let $C$ be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a perfect field $k$, and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module with dual $\mathcal L^{-1}$ (def-invertible-sheaf). Write $\omega_C=\Omega^1_{C/k}$ for the canonical bundle (def-canonical-line-bundle-curve) and $\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L$ for the sheaf of principal parts of $\mathcal L$ (def-principal-parts-sheaf-line-bundle-curve). Tensoring with the dual gives the invertible sheaf $\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1}$ (def-sheaf-tensor-product, def-sheaf-hom). **Local pairing.** Let $c_p\in\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p$ be a local principal part of $\mathcal L$ at a closed point $p$, and let $s\in(\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})_p$ be a regular local section of the dual twist. Their product is a rational differential, defined modulo regular differentials at $p$: if $c_p$ is represented by $\widetilde c_p\in\mathcal L_\eta$, then $\widetilde c_p s$ is a rational differential. Replacing $\widetilde c_p$ by another representative changes it by an element of $\mathcal L_p$, whose product with $s$ is in $\omega_{C,p}$ and is regular. Thus the local residue $\operatorname{res}_p(c_p s)$ of def-residue-rational-differential-curve-point is independent of the representative of $c_p$. In a local trivialization with parameter $t$, this is the residue of the Laurent expansion of $\widetilde c_p s$; only its $t^{-1}dt$ coefficient is used. **The pairing.** Let $c=(c_p)$ be a finite-support family of local principal parts of $\mathcal L$; such families represent the classes of $H^1(C,\mathcal L)$, namely $H^1(C,\mathcal L)$ is the cokernel of the diagonal map $\mathcal L_\eta\to\bigoplus_p\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p$ (lem-principal-parts-cech-h1-presentation). Let $s$ be a global section of $\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1}$. Define $$\langle c,s\rangle:=\sum_{p}\operatorname{res}_p(c_p\,s)\in k .$$ The sum is finite: $c_p=0$ for all but finitely many $p$ by finite support, and therefore $\operatorname{res}_p(c_p s)=0$ for all but finitely many $p$; a global section $s$ is regular at every closed point, so no further poles appear. The construction is $k$-linear in the family $c$ and in the section $s$, by the $k$-linearity of the local residue and of the tensor product. This defines the **residue pairing** on pairs of representatives, $$\langle\;,\;\rangle\colon\Bigl(\text{finite-support families in }\textstyle\bigoplus_p\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p\Bigr)\times H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})\longrightarrow k .$$ It is independent of the chosen representative of the principal-part family: a new representative differs by the principal parts of a global meromorphic section of $\mathcal L$ and by a family of local regular sections, and the independence is the descent statement proved in the next item of this development, which yields the induced $k$-bilinear pairing $$H^1(C,\mathcal L)\times H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})\to k .$$

items.title: The residue pairing is well defined on cohomology
items.statement: Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a perfect field k, L an invertible sheaf and s a global section of omega_C tensor L^{-1}. Then the functional c -> sum_p res_p(c_p s) on finite-support families of local L-principal parts (def-residue-pairing-principal-parts) vanishes on the principal parts of global rational sections of L and on families of local regular sections, hence descends to a k-linear functional H^1(C,L) -> k. Consequently the residue pairing < , > : H^1(C,L) x H^0(C, omega_C tensor L^{-1}) -> k is well defined, k-bilinear and functorial in L, and the fact that it is independent of the representing family is exactly the content of the global residue theorem for the rational differential theta s obtained from a global rational section theta of L.

items.strategy: Two representatives of the same class in H^1(C,L) differ by the principal parts of a global rational section theta of L and by a family of local regular sections of L. A local regular section c_p lies in L_p, so c_p s lies in the regular differentials at p and has residue zero; this uses only the definition of the residue and vanishing of residues of regular differentials. For the rational section theta, the sum of residues of theta s is zero by the global residue theorem; theta s is a global rational differential and its local principal parts are exactly theta_p s_p, so the change of representative changes the pairing by zero. The statement of well-definedness is thus exactly the global residue theorem applied to the rational differential obtained by multiplying a rational section of L by s.

items.title: Functoriality of the residue pairing under line-bundle maps and connecting homomorphisms
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the residue suppliers. Let $C$ be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a perfect field $k$ and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module. The residue pairing of def-residue-pairing-principal-parts is functorial in the following sense. (1) *Multiplicativity in the line bundle.* Let $\mathcal M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module and let $t\in H^0(C,\mathcal M)$ be a nonzero global section. Multiplication of representatives by $t$ induces a $k$-linear map $$\mu_t\colon H^1(C,\mathcal L)\longrightarrow H^1(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M);$$ if $s\in H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})$ is a global section whose associated rational section $s\otimes t^{-1}$ of $\omega_C\otimes(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)^{-1}$ is regular at every closed point, then $$\bigl\langle\mu_t(c),\,s\otimes t^{-1}\bigr\rangle_{\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M} =\langle c,s\rangle_{\mathcal L}$$ for every $c\in H^1(C,\mathcal L)$. If $t$ is nowhere vanishing, then $s\otimes t^{-1}$ is a global section of $\omega_C\otimes(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)^{-1}$ for every $s$ and $\mu_t$ is an isomorphism that identifies the two residue pairings. (2) *Adjunction with the connecting homomorphism.* Let $D$ be an effective Cartier divisor on $C$, put $\mathcal L'=\mathcal L(D)\cong \mathcal L\otimes\mathcal O_C(D)$, and let $$0\longrightarrow\mathcal L\longrightarrow\mathcal L'\longrightarrow i_*(\mathcal L'|_D)\longrightarrow 0$$ be the associated exact sequence, obtained locally from an equation of $D$, with quotient supported on $D$ and connecting homomorphism $\delta\colon H^0(C,i_*(\mathcal L'|_D))\to H^1(C,\mathcal L)$. Then for every $g\in H^0(C,i_*(\mathcal L'|_D))$ and every $s\in H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})$ one has $$\langle\delta(g),s\rangle_{\mathcal L} =\sum_{p\in\operatorname{supp}D}\operatorname{res}_p(\tilde g_ps),$$ where $\tilde g_p\in\mathcal L'_p$ is any local lift of the germ $g_p$ of $g$ at $p$. The right-hand side is independent of the lifts and defines a restriction map $\rho_D\colon H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})\to H^0(C,i_*(\mathcal L'|_D))^*$ by $\rho_D(s)(g)=\sum_p\operatorname{res}_p(\tilde g_ps)$. The connecting map $\delta$ is adjoint to $\rho_D$ under the residue pairing. Moreover, $\ker\rho_D$ is the image of the natural inclusion $H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L'^{-1})\hookrightarrow H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})$. Together with (1) this is the compatibility with the standard exact sequences that pins down the pairing once the trace normalization on $\omega_C$ is fixed.

items.strategy: Compute multiplicativity on finite-support representatives. Identify the effective-divisor connecting map with local principal-part lifts through the natural exact-sequence diagram; prove lift independence because differences multiply to regular differentials. For the kernel of the adjoint restriction, test each coefficient up to the divisor multiplicity using residue-field trace-dual tests.

items.title: Annihilators of regular sections under the local residue pairing
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the residue suppliers. Let $C$ be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a perfect field $k$, let $p$ be a closed point with uniformizer $t$, and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module. Write $\omega_C$ for the canonical bundle and consider the local residue pairing $$\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p\;\times\;(\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})_p\longrightarrow k,\qquad (c,s)\longmapsto \operatorname{res}_p(cs),$$ where $\mathcal L_\eta$ is the sheaf of rational sections of $\mathcal L$. Then: 1. the annihilator of the image of the regular sections $(\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})_p$ inside $\mathcal L_\eta$ is exactly $\mathcal L_p$: an element $c\in\mathcal L_\eta$ satisfies $\operatorname{res}_p(cs)=0$ for every $s\in(\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})_p$ if and only if $c\in\mathcal L_p$, so the induced pairing on $\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p$ is nondegenerate on the left; dually the annihilator of $\mathcal L_p$ inside the space $(\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})_\eta$ of rational sections is the image of the regular sections: an element $s\in(\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})_\eta$ satisfies $\operatorname{res}_p(cs)=0$ for every $c\in\mathcal L_p$ if and only if $s\in(\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})_p$; 2. after a local trivialization and completion, each nonzero pole in either factor is detected by a complementary finite Laurent coefficient and the nondegenerate trace form of $\kappa(p)/k$; these coefficient tests prove the two annihilator statements in every characteristic.

references.title: John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159
MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025), Chs. 19 and 21

items.strategy: Work with the actual DVR and its completion without identifying them. Lift the needed residue-field coefficient to O_{C,p}; the leading negative Laurent coefficient is detected by the nondegenerate trace form. Reverse the test for a rational dual section. These finite coefficient tests establish the annihilators without claims about algebraic duals of completed series spaces.

items.title: A nonzero global dual section detects a cohomology class
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the residue suppliers. Let $C$
be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a perfect field $k$ and
let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module. Then the $k$-linear
map
$$\Phi\colon H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})\longrightarrow H^1(C,\mathcal L)^*,\qquad s\longmapsto\bigl(c\mapsto\langle c,s\rangle\bigr),$$
given by the residue pairing of [[def-residue-pairing-principal-parts]] is
injective: every nonzero global section $s$ of
$\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1}$ detects some class in $H^1(C,\mathcal L)$.
If, in addition, the two spaces are known to be finite-dimensional of equal
dimension (the dimension balance established separately in this development),
then $\Phi$ is an isomorphism. Under that additional hypothesis the residue
pairing is perfect: the annihilator in $H^1(C,\mathcal L)$ of all global dual
sections is zero. By the principal-parts presentation, any finite-support
representative of such a class then lies in the diagonal image of a global
rational section of $\mathcal L$.

references.title: John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159
MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25

items.strategy: For nonzero s, use localization of a frame to show its generic and closed-point germs are nonzero. Obtain a closed point from a strict chain Z0 subsetneq Z1 of nonempty irreducible closed subsets in the dimension-one curve, then apply lem-curve-closed-subsets-finite to Z0. At p write s=u(dt tensor e_L^{-1}); factor u=t^n v by the DVR normal form before defining n and v. Nondegeneracy of the finite separable trace form gives b with Tr(b v(0)) nonzero. Lift b to a local unit and test with the principal part u_b t^{-(n+1)}e_L. Its product with s has coefficient t^{-1}(u_b v), whose t^{-1} coefficient is b v(0), proving injectivity. Perfectness and the annihilator conclusion still require the separate finite equal-dimension hypothesis.

items.title: The twisting sheaf of projective space is very ample and ample
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the projective-space suppliers. Let k be a field and n >= 0. The twisting sheaf O_{P^n_k}(1) is closed H-very ample relative to Spec k: the identity is a closed immersion id: P^n_k -> P^n_k with id^*O(1) isomorphic to O(1) (def-very-ample-invertible-sheaf-relative). Consequently O_{P^n_k}(1) is ample on P^n_k (lem-very-ample-implies-ample), every positive tensor power O(d), d >= 1, is ample (lem-ample-stable-positive-power), and for every finite morphism g: Y -> P^n_k the pullback g^*O(1) is an ample invertible sheaf on Y (lem-ample-pullback-finite-morphism).

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)

items.strategy: The identity morphism of P^n_k is a closed immersion; the definition of closed H-very ampleness relative to Spec k asks for a closed immersion i with L isomorphic to i^*O(1), and the identity morpism satisfies i^*O(1) = O(1). Hence O(1) is closed H-very ample, and lem-very-ample-implies-ample makes it ample. Positive powers: O(d) = O(1)^{tensor d}, and ampleness is stable under positive powers (lem-ample-stable-positive-power); alternatively the d-th Veronese description exhibits O(d) as very ample directly. The pullback statement is lem-ample-pullback-finite-morphism.

items.title: Every smooth proper curve admits a projective embedding
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the rational-function, projective-space and finite-morphism suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field k. Then there is an integer N >= 0 and a closed immersion i: C -> P^N_k over k; equivalently the structure morphism C -> Spec k is projective in the H-projective convention of def-projective-morphism-pre-proj. The proof uses no Serre duality, no Riemann-Roch and no residue theory, so this corollary may be used by the duality items of this page without circularity.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
Joseph Lipman, Residues, duality, and the fundamental class of a scheme-map (2011)
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)

items.strategy: Derive trdeg k(C)=1 from an affine chart through a closed point and the smooth local DVR. All curve local rings are integrally closed; choose a transcendental rational function and apply the normal-proper-curve finite-map lemma. Pull back ample O_P1(1) along the finite morphism, then apply ample powers over the Noetherian field base to obtain a closed H-projective embedding. No Riemann-Roch, residue or duality result is used.

items.title: The two sides of the residue pairing have the same dimension
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the duality suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a perfect field k and let L be an invertible sheaf on C. Then dim_k H^1(C,L) = dim_k H^0(C, omega_C tensor L^{-1}); both spaces are finite-dimensional and the equality is the numerical form of Serre duality for L, obtained from the published duality theorem for smooth projective varieties after cor-projective-embedding-every-smooth-proper-curve makes C projective. Combined with lem-global-residue-pairing-injective-left this shows that the residue pairing of def-residue-pairing-principal-parts is a perfect pairing over perfect k.

references.title: John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25

items.strategy: Apply the published smooth-projective Serre duality theorem to X = C of pure dimension n = 1 and E = L, a finite locally free module of rank one: for q = 1 it pairs H^1(C,L) perfectly with H^0(C, L^{-1} tensor omega_C), hence the two k-vector spaces have equal finite dimension. Together with the injectivity of lem-global-residue-pairing-injective-left, which exhibits H^0(C, omega_C tensor L^{-1}) as a subspace of the dual of H^1(C,L) of the same dimension as H^1(C,L), the residue pairing is a perfect pairing: injectivity plus equal finite dimensions makes the map an isomorphism of vector spaces. The alternative induction on divisors over a perfect field would reprove the numerical statement without invoking the projective duality theorem, but the published theorem is available here and is exactly the AV-25 route prescribed by the design.

items.title: Serre duality for line bundles on a smooth proper curve, and the residue realization
items.statement: Assume AC. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over k and L an invertible sheaf. (1) Over arbitrary k, C is projective and the published smooth-projective theorem gives the fixed, embedding-independent Gysin trace t_C and the functorial perfect pairing H¹(C,L) × H⁰(C,ω_C⊗L⁻¹) → k, (c,s) ↦ t_C(c∪s). (2) Over perfect k, t_C(ξ) = −Σ_p res_p(ξ_p). For every L and s ∈ H⁰(C,ω_C⊗L⁻¹), t_C(c∪s) = −⟨c,s⟩ = −Σ_p res_p(c_p s). Hence the positive residue pairing is perfect, bilinear, and functorial, and h¹(C,L)=h⁰(C,ω_C⊗L⁻¹).

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
John Tate, Residues of differentials on curves, Ann. Sci. E.N.S. (4) 1 (1968) 149-159
Joseph Lipman, Residues, duality, and the fundamental class of a scheme-map (2011)

items.strategy: Specialize published smooth-projective duality for the arbitrary-field fixed-trace pairing. Over perfect k, compare trace and positive residues on a trace-detecting closed-point boundary after separable extension. For a rational point the Cartier extension has raw cocycle +du and the normalized trace-one point class has −du. Prove their comparison globally on C with the one-point sheaf-Ext-to-global-Ext spectral sequence: the Cartier-point locally free resolution computes sheaf Ext, the injective Hom double complex computes that resolution, and the only nonzero Ext sheaf is acyclic one-point support. The positive Yoneda boundary is therefore the negative normalized class, with one sign conversion, so t_C is − the residue sum. Cartier-twist connecting-map naturality then gives the negative residue pairing; perfectness and dimensions are unchanged.

items.title: Serre duality for finite locally free sheaves on a smooth proper curve
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the duality suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field k and let E be a finite locally free O_C-module of rank r. Then there is a functorial perfect k-bilinear pairing H^1(C,E) x H^0(C, E^v tensor omega_C) -> k given by c cup s followed by the normalized trace t_C: H^1(C, omega_C) -> k, and consequently a canonical k-linear isomorphism H^1(C,E)^* isomorphic to H^0(C, E^v tensor omega_C) and the dimension identity h^1(C,E) = h^0(C, E^v tensor omega_C). For E of rank one this recovers thm-serre-duality-curves-line-bundles, and the result is stated over an arbitrary field with no perfectness hypothesis.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
Joseph Lipman, Residues, duality, and the fundamental class of a scheme-map (2011)

items.strategy: Specialize the published smooth-projective Serre duality theorem to X = C, which has pure dimension 1 and is projective by cor-projective-embedding-every-smooth-proper-curve, and to the finite locally free module E; take q = 1. The theorem gives the perfect pairing between H^1(C,E) and H^0(C, E^v tensor omega_C) with value in H^1(C, omega_C), followed by the normalized trace. Functoriality and the isomorphism statement are part of the cited theorem; taking E of rank one recovers the line-bundle case of thm-serre-duality-curves-line-bundles. No perfectness of k is needed in this item.

items.title: Serre duality for coherent sheaves on a smooth proper curve, Ext form
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the duality and coherent-cohomology suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over an arbitrary field k and let F be a coherent O_C-module. Then there are canonical k-linear isomorphisms Hom_{O_C}(F, omega_C) isomorphic to H^1(C,F)^* and Ext^1_{O_C}(F, omega_C) isomorphic to H^0(C,F)^*, both functorial in F, where Ext is the global sheaf Ext of def-sheaf-ext-for-coherent-modules. In particular h^1(C,F) = dim_k Hom_{O_C}(F, omega_C) for every coherent F, and for F finite locally free the first isomorphism is the vector-bundle duality of thm-serre-duality-curves-vector-bundles.

references.title: Joseph Lipman, Residues, duality, and the fundamental class of a scheme-map (2011)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25

items.strategy: Construct a two-term locally free resolution using a projective embedding, ample twist, finite global generation and a torsion-free kernel. Define canonical Hom/H1 and Ext1/H0 pairings by composition with the fixed normalized trace. Prove global Ext/vector-bundle cohomology comparison via tensor adjunction and flasque injectives; use a kernel comparison for Hom, then an aligned five-lemma diagram for Ext1. Prove the middle square with the injective-resolution pushout/pullback calculation and its positive connecting sign. Preserve all coherent sheaves and arbitrary field.

items.title: h^1 of a line bundle equals the space of dual sections
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the duality suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field k, let K_C be a canonical divisor and let D be a divisor on C. Then h^1(C, O_C(D)) = h^0(C, O_C(K_C - D)) = l(K_C - D), i.e. the index of speciality of D equals the dimension of the space of sections of the dual twist, and the full Riemann-Roch identity may accordingly be written l(D) - l(K_C - D) = deg_k(D) + 1 - g with no unknown term.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
Joseph Lipman, Residues, duality, and the fundamental class of a scheme-map (2011)

items.strategy: Apply fixed-trace line-bundle duality and the canonical Cartier tensor/inverse dictionary; obtain i(D)=l(K_C-D), then explicitly substitute it in thm-riemann-roch-as-l-minus-index to prove the promised full RR identity.

items.title: The full Riemann-Roch theorem for divisors on a smooth proper curve
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the coherent-cohomology suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field k with genus g = g(C) and canonical divisor K_C (the divisor of a nonzero rational differential, def-canonical-line-bundle-curve). Then for every divisor D on C, l(D) - l(K_C - D) = deg_k(D) + 1 - g, equivalently h^0(C, O_C(D)) - h^1(C, O_C(D)) is the Euler characteristic and i(D) = h^1(C,O_C(D)) = l(K_C - D). Both sides are unchanged if K_C is replaced by a linearly equivalent canonical divisor.

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Ch. 8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25

items.strategy: thm-riemann-roch-as-l-minus-index gives l(D) - i(D) = deg_k(D) + 1 - g where i(D) = h^1(C, O_C(D)) is the index of speciality. cor-h1-line-bundle-dual-sections identifies h^1(C, O_C(D)) with h^0(C, omega_C tensor O_C(-D)), and the divisor/sheaf dictionary (def-canonical-line-bundle-curve, lem-rational-differential-divisor-well-defined-class, thm-cartier-weil-divisors-curves-agree) identifies omega_C tensor O_C(-D) with O_C(K_C - D), so i(D) = l(K_C - D). Substituting gives the stated identity; no perfectness of k and no residue theory is used. Linearly equivalent canonical divisors differ by a principal divisor, hence give the same line bundle and the same space of sections.

items.title: The canonical bundle has exactly g independent sections
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the duality and coherent-cohomology suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field k of genus g with canonical bundle omega_C. Then h^0(C, omega_C) = g and h^1(C, O_C) = g; equivalently l(K_C) = g for any canonical divisor K_C.

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Ch. 8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25

items.strategy: The genus is h1(O_C) by definition; line-bundle duality identifies it with h0(omega_C), and the canonical divisor dictionary yields l(K_C)=g. No Euler-RR invocation is needed.

items.title: The canonical divisor has degree 2g - 2
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the duality suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field k of genus g with canonical divisor K_C. Then deg_k(K_C) = 2g - 2, independently of the choice of the nonzero rational differential defining K_C.

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Ch. 8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25

items.strategy: Apply the full Riemann-Roch identity to D = K_C: l(K_C) - l(0) = deg_k(K_C) + 1 - g. Here l(0) = h^0(C, O_C) = 1 by thm-h0-structure-sheaf-proper-curve, and l(K_C) = h^0(C, omega_C) = g by cor-h0-canonical-differentials-genus. Hence g - 1 = deg_k(K_C) + 1 - g, that is deg_k(K_C) = 2g - 2. Two canonical divisors are linearly equivalent (lem-rational-differential-divisor-well-defined-class), so they have equal degree.

items.title: H^1 of a line bundle vanishes above degree 2g - 2
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the duality suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field k of genus g and let L be an invertible O_C-module with deg(L) > 2g - 2. Then H^1(C, L) = 0 and h^0(C, L) = deg(L) + 1 - g.

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Ch. 8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25

items.strategy: Write L = O_C(D) with deg_k(D) = deg(L) (thm-cartier-weil-divisors-curves-agree and the degree definition on curves). By cor-h1-line-bundle-dual-sections, h^1(C, L) = l(K_C - D). Now deg_k(K_C - D) = deg_k(K_C) - deg_k(D) = (2g - 2) - deg(L) < 0 by cor-canonical-degree-two-g-minus-two, and an invertible sheaf of negative degree has no nonzero global section (thm-degree-positive-line-bundle-sections-zero-bound), so l(K_C - D) = 0 and H^1(C, L) = 0. Then l(D) - 0 = deg_k(D) + 1 - g by the Riemann-Roch identity of thm-riemann-roch-as-l-minus-index.

items.title: Riemann-Roch in exact form for divisors of degree above 2g - 2
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the duality suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field k of genus g and let D be a divisor with deg_k(D) > 2g - 2. Then l(D) = deg_k(D) + 1 - g, i.e. D is nonspecial in the sense of def-nonspecial-divisor, and h^1(C, O_C(D)) = 0.

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Ch. 8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25

items.strategy: The vanishing corollary applied to L = O_C(D) gives h^1(C, O_C(D)) = 0, and the Riemann-Roch identity l(D) - i(D) = deg_k(D) + 1 - g with i(D) = 0 gives l(D) = deg_k(D) + 1 - g. Equivalently, the full Riemann-Roch form l(D) - l(K_C - D) = deg_k(D) + 1 - g reduces to l(D) = deg_k(D) + 1 - g because deg_k(K_C - D) < 0 forces l(K_C - D) = 0. By definition a divisor with h^1 = 0 is nonspecial (def-nonspecial-divisor).

items.title: Line bundles of degree at least 2g are base-point-free
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the duality suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field k of genus g and let L be an invertible O_C-module with deg(L) >= 2g. Then L is base-point-free: for every closed point p of C there is a global section s of L with s not vanishing at p; equivalently the evaluation morphism O_C^{h^0(C,L)} -> L is surjective, and the complete linear system |L| defines a k-morphism phi_L: C -> P^{h^0(C,L)-1}_k with phi_L^*O(1) isomorphic to L. Over an algebraically closed field the sharper statement h^0(C,L)-h^0(C,L(-p))=1 holds at every closed point p.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Ch. 8
MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25

items.strategy: Prove degree preservation under arbitrary field extension by decomposing the residue algebra into Artinian local factors and reading their lengths as pulled-back divisor coefficients. Over the algebraic closure, use high-degree Riemann–Roch and the point exact sequence to generate every stalk, then descend evaluation surjectivity and form the complete-system morphism.

items.title: Line bundles of degree at least 2g+1 are very ample
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the duality and projective-space suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field k of genus g and let L be an invertible O_C-module with deg(L) >= 2g+1. Then L is very ample: L is closed H-very ample relative to Spec k in the sense of def-very-ample-invertible-sheaf-relative, and the base-point-free morphism phi_L: C -> P^{h^0(C,L)-1}_k of thm-base-point-free-linear-system-morphism is a closed immersion with phi_L^*O(1) isomorphic to L.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Ch. 8
MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25

items.strategy: Preserve degree under arbitrary field extension, then use Riemann–Roch over the algebraic closure to separate geometric points and first jets. Over each field, prove the proper map finite through its integral one-dimensional scheme image, finite function-field extension, and isolated-fibre criterion; use tangent and cotangent maps plus Nakayama for closed-immersion surjectivity, then descend faithfully flatly.

items.title: Hyperelliptic curves and hyperelliptic maps
items.statement: **Choice premise.** The definitions of hyperelliptic and geometrically hyperelliptic are unconditional. Assume AC for all proved assertions below: the map-finiteness and function-to-map, global-sections, projective-space, Čech-comparison, long-exact-sequence, Riemann--Roch, Serre-duality, and birational-curve suppliers used here explicitly require it ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[lem-function-with-poles-defines-map-p1]], [[thm-nonconstant-morphism-proper-curves-finite-surjective]], [[thm-h0-structure-sheaf-proper-curve]], [[thm-projective-map-line-bundle-data-equivalence]], [[thm-cohomology-projective-space-twisting-sheaves]], [[thm-cech-computes-qc-cohomology-separated-scheme-affine-cover]], [[thm-long-exact-sequence-sheaf-cohomology]], [[thm-full-riemann-roch-divisor]], [[thm-serre-duality-curves-line-bundles]], [[cor-canonical-degree-two-g-minus-two]], [[cor-h0-canonical-differentials-genus]], [[cor-birational-smooth-proper-curves-isomorphic]]). Let $k$ be a field and let $C$ be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over $k$ ([[def-algebraic-curve-over-field]]) of genus $g$. A $k$-morphism $$\phi:C\longrightarrow\mathbf P^1_k$$ is a **hyperelliptic map** on $C$ when it is nonconstant of degree two, $\deg\phi=2$ in the sense of [[def-nonconstant-morphism-curves-degree]], with target the projective line $\mathbf P^1_k$ in its standard charts ([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]]). Such a morphism is finite. The curve $C$ is **hyperelliptic over $k$** when it admits such a map; this means that the degree-two target is the split projective line over $k$. The curve is **geometrically hyperelliptic** when $C_{\bar k}=C\times_k\bar k$ admits a degree-two map to $\mathbf P^1_{\bar k}$, where $\bar k$ is an algebraic closure. These definitions impose no restriction on the genus or characteristic. A geometrically hyperelliptic curve need not be hyperelliptic over $k$: its degree-two quotient can descend to a nonsplit genus-zero curve rather than to $\mathbf P^1_k$. For every genus, a nonconstant rational function $f\in k(C)^\times$ gives a finite map $\phi_f:C\to\mathbf P^1_k$ of degree $[k(C):k(f)]$, with pole divisor the fibre over infinity ([[lem-function-with-poles-defines-map-p1]]). Thus $C$ is hyperelliptic over $k$ if and only if some nonconstant $f\in k(C)^\times$ has $[k(C):k(f)]=2$; every hyperelliptic map is obtained this way, up to an automorphism of $\mathbf P^1_k$. If $g\ge1$, then hyperellipticity over $k$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{gon}(C)=2$, where gonality is the minimum degree of a nonconstant $k$-map to $\mathbf P^1_k$ ([[def-gonality-curve]]). Indeed, a degree-one map between smooth proper curves is an isomorphism, so would force $C\cong\mathbf P^1_k$ and $g=0$; conversely, a gonality of two is attained by a map of degree two. This equivalence is not asserted in genus zero: $\mathbf P^1_k$ itself has degree-two self-maps and gonality one. For every field $k$ and every $g\ge1$, the following is also equivalent to hyperellipticity over $k$: there is an invertible sheaf $L$ on $C$ ([[def-invertible-sheaf]]) of degree two with $h^0(C,L)=2$ whose complete linear system is base-point-free. A hyperelliptic map gives $L=\phi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}(1)$; the section count is proved below. Conversely, a basis of the two sections of such an $L$ gives a nonconstant map $C\to\mathbf P^1_k$, and the degree of its fibre over a rational point is $\deg L=2$, so it is a hyperelliptic map. The genus qualification is necessary: on $\mathbf P^1$ the pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$ under a degree-two map is $\mathcal O(2)$, with three sections. For $g\ge2$, any two hyperelliptic maps over $k$ are related by a $k$-automorphism of $\mathbf P^1_k$. The proof below is over the given field; it does not infer a split-target map from geometric hyperellipticity.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Ch. 8
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)

items.strategy: Define hyperellipticity over k by a finite degree-two map to the split projective line, and distinguish geometric hyperellipticity after base change. Prove the degree-two line-bundle criterion using the finite rank-two direct image, its quotient line bundle and the two-chart cohomology calculation; prove the converse from a base-point-free pencil. For g >= 2, use Riemann--Roch and duality to identify L^(g-1) with omega_C and the canonical Veronese factorization to prove uniqueness over the given field.

items.title: The canonical map: base-point-freeness and the hyperelliptic exception
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the duality suppliers. Let $C$ be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field $k$ of genus $g\ge2$, with canonical bundle $\omega_C$ and canonical divisor $K_C$. 1. $\omega_C$ is generated by its global sections, so the canonical map $\phi_K:C\to\mathbf P^{g-1}_k$ is a $k$-morphism with $\phi_K^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\omega_C$, and the divisors of the canonical system are the pullbacks of hyperplanes under $\phi_K$. 2. $\phi_K$ is a closed immersion if and only if $g\ge3$ and $C$ is geometrically nonhyperelliptic, meaning $C_{\bar k}$ admits no degree-two map to $\mathbf P^1_{\bar k}$. 3. If $C$ is hyperelliptic over $k$ with map $\phi:C\to\mathbf P^1_k$ and $L=\phi^*\mathcal O(1)$, then $L^{\otimes(g-1)}\cong\omega_C$, and $\phi_K$ factors through the $(g-1)$st Veronese embedding of $\mathbf P^1_k$. More generally this factorization holds over $\bar k$ for every geometrically hyperelliptic $C$. In either case the canonical map has generic degree two onto a rational normal curve and is not a closed immersion.

items.strategy: Base-change to an algebraic closure for point and tangent separation. Use duality and Riemann--Roch to turn each failure into a degree-one or degree-two map; prove the canonical morphism finite and use the finite local-ring/Nakayama argument for a closed immersion. Analyze hyperelliptic Veronese factorization, rule out purely inseparable degree-two maps in characteristic two, and descend the closed immersion over k.

items.title: Adjunction for smooth plane curves
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the duality and projective-space suppliers. Let k be a field, d >= 1, and let F in k[x_0,x_1,x_2] be a homogeneous form of degree d such that the plane curve C = V_+(F) in P^2_k is smooth of pure dimension one (equivalently, the dehomogenisations of F are square-free with no common zero with their partials). Then the canonical bundle of C satisfies omega_C = Omega^1_{C/k} isomorphic to O_C(d-3), where O_C(m) is the restriction of O_{P^2_k}(m); consequently every canonical divisor of C is linearly equivalent to the divisor of a nonzero rational section of O_C(d-3).
