Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)

items.strategy: The multiplication-by-F sequence 0 -> O_{P^2}(-d) -> O_{P^2} -> i_*O_C -> 0 of lem-projective-hypersurface-cohomology-sequence identifies C with Proj k[x_0,x_1,x_2]/(F) and identifies its ideal sheaf I with O_{P^2}(-d); since a hyperplane class section of a curve of degree d has degree d, the conormal sheaf I/I^2 is isomorphic to i^*O_{P^2}(-d) = O_C(-d), invertible of rank one (lem-projective-hypersurface-affine-pieces; for the general regular-immersion conormal description, lem-smooth-closed-immersion-regular-conormal-sequence). The adjunction isomorphism of lem-smooth-closed-subvariety-dualizing-line-bundle-adjunction for the closed immersion C -> P^2 reads omega_C isomorphic to omega_{P^2}|_C tensor det(N_{C/P^2}), and in codimension one det(N) = N = (I/I^2)^{dual} isomorphic to O_C(d). The dualizing bundle of P^2 is O(-3) (def-smooth-projective-dualizing-line-bundle-and-trace and thm-serre-duality-projective-space-twisting-sheaves), so omega_C is isomorphic to O_C(-3) tensor O_C(d) = O_C(d-3). Smoothness of C is exactly the hypothesis that makes the closed immersion regular, so the conormal sheaf is invertible.

items.title: The genus of a smooth plane curve in terms of its degree
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from curve divisor and DVR theory, duality and adjunction, projective properness, dimension, Jacobian, and Bezout suppliers. Let $C=V_+(F)\subseteq\mathbf P^2_k$ be a smooth plane curve of degree $d\ge1$ over a field $k$. Then the genus of $C$ is $$g(C)=\frac{(d-1)(d-2)}{2};$$ in particular a smooth plane cubic has genus one and a smooth plane quartic has genus three.

items.strategy: derive geometric integrality from smoothness using the actual local hypersurface equations, compute the hyperplane degree by weighted Bezout, and then apply adjunction and $\deg\omega_C=2g-2$.

items.title: Fibres, pullbacks and degrees of divisors under a finite morphism of curves
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the DVR and finite-morphism suppliers. Let f: C -> D be a nonconstant morphism of smooth proper geometrically integral curves over a field k, n = deg(f). Then f is finite and flat, so the pullback f^*E of a Cartier (equivalently Weil) divisor is defined; for a closed point q of D one has f^*[q] = sum over p in f^{-1}(q) of e_p [p] as a divisor on C, where e_p is the ramification index of f at p (def-ramification-index-curve-map); and for every divisor E on D, deg_k(f^*E) = n deg_k(E). Consequently, for every invertible O_D-module M, deg(f^*M) = n deg(M).

items.strategy: Use nonconstant proper curve morphism finiteness and dominance. Closed source points map to closed target points by finite closedness; their local ring maps are injective and the source DVR is torsion-free over the target DVR, hence flat by the PID criterion without finite-generation of individual stalks. Generic stalks are field extensions and flat, proving stalkwise flatness. Pull back effective point Cartier charts, read cycle coefficients as ramification orders, and use weighted fibre-degree and residue tower laws. Extend additively to signed divisors and transfer to line bundles by the actual Cartier pullback isomorphism. AC implies the DC needed for the cycle map.

items.title: The Riemann-Hurwitz formula with the different
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the ramification and duality suppliers. Let f: C -> D be a finite surjective morphism of smooth proper geometrically integral curves over a field k whose function-field extension k(C)/k(D) is separable (equivalently, a nonconstant morphism whose generic fibre is separable), with n = deg(f) and different divisor R_f (def-different-divisor-curve-map). Then 2g(C) - 2 = n (2g(D) - 2) + deg_k(R_f), where g(C), g(D) are the genera. Equivalently, for canonical divisors, K_C is linearly equivalent to f^*K_D + R_f and the displayed identity is the degree identity obtained from it.

Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)

items.strategy: The canonical-bundle formula of thm-canonical-bundle-ramification-formula gives a canonical isomorphism omega_C isomorphic to f^*omega_D tensor O_C(R_f). Degrees of invertible sheaves are additive under tensor product of the corresponding divisors, so deg_k omega_C = deg_k(f^*omega_D) + deg_k(R_f). The middle term is n deg_k omega_D by lem-degree-pullback-divisor-finite-morphism-curves (which uses the fibre-degree sum and flatness of the finite map), and the outer terms are 2g(C) - 2 and 2g(D) - 2 by cor-canonical-degree-two-g-minus-two. Substituting gives 2g(C) - 2 = n(2g(D) - 2) + deg_k R_f. The divisor form follows by comparing the isomorphism omega_C = O_C(K_C) with f^*O_D(K_D) tensor O_C(R_f) = O_C(f^*K_D + R_f) via thm-cartier-weil-divisors-curves-agree. No duality beyond the degree of the canonical divisor is used, and the separability hypothesis is exactly the one required by the canonical ramification formula; the inseparable theory through the different of the residue extensions is not invoked here.

items.title: The genus relation for unramified covers of curves
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the ramification suppliers. Let f: C -> D be a finite etale morphism of smooth proper geometrically integral curves over a field k (equivalently a finite surjective morphism that is flat and unramified at every point), with n = deg(f). Then 2g(C) - 2 = n(2g(D) - 2), i.e. the different vanishes and the Euler characteristic 2 - 2g is multiplied by n.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Ch. 8
The Stacks Project, Algebraic Curves (tag 0BRV)

items.strategy: A finite etale morphism is unramified at every point, and unramifiedness at a closed point p of C means e_p = 1 with separable residue extension (def-ramification-and-branch-points), so the local length l_p = length(Omega_{C/D,p}) vanishes by lem-curve-different-local-support-and-index-bound; hence the different divisor R_f = sum l_p [p] is zero. The generic fibre is a finite etale algebra over the function field k(D), so the function-field extension is separable, and thm-riemann-hurwitz-complete applies with deg R_f = 0, giving 2g(C) - 2 = n(2g(D) - 2). This completes the genus relation left open on the smooth-proper-curves page, where only the base-change-monotonicity form of the statement was available.

items.title: The canonical bundle of a genus-one curve is trivial
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the duality suppliers. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field k of genus g = 1. Then omega_C is isomorphic to O_C, every canonical divisor is principal, and h^0(C, omega_C) = 1. No rational point of C is needed.

references.title: William Fulton, Algebraic Curves (Internet Archive copy), Ch. 8
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea (version of October 21, 2025)
MIT 18.725 Algebraic Geometry (Fall 2015) course notes, Lectures 24-25

items.strategy: deg omega_C = 2g - 2 = 0 by cor-canonical-degree-two-g-minus-two, and h^0(C, omega_C) = g = 1 by cor-h0-canonical-differentials-genus, so omega_C has a nonzero global section. An invertible sheaf of degree zero with a nonzero global section is trivial (cor-degree-zero-line-bundle-section-trivial), so omega_C is isomorphic to O_C, and a canonical divisor, being the divisor of a section, is principal. The design states the theorem for genus-one curves with a rational point; the rational point is not used by this route, and the stronger statement is recorded here.

items.title: A genus-one curve embeds as a plane cubic
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from cohomology, linear systems, smooth-curve DVR and divisor theory, projective-space, affine-dimension, and Bezout suppliers. Let $C$ be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve of genus one over a field $k$ that has a rational point $p_0$ (equivalently, a degree-one divisor), and let $L$ be an invertible sheaf of degree three on $C$, for instance $L=\mathcal O_C(3p_0)$. Then $h^0(C,L)=3$, the sheaf $L$ is very ample, and $\phi_L:C\to\mathbf P^2_k$ is a closed immersion whose image is a plane cubic curve, that is, a curve of degree three in $\mathbf P^2_k$; in particular every genus-one curve with a rational point is isomorphic to a plane cubic.

items.title: Normalization of the trace for Serre duality on a curve
items.statement: For a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over perfect k, t_C is the fixed projective Gysin trace and t_C(ξ)=−Σ_p res_p(ξ_p). At a rational split point, the Cartier-extension class has raw local cocycle +du and the normalized trace-one point class has −du. The one-point sheaf-Ext-to-global-Ext comparison on C identifies these as opposite global Ext classes; the positive Yoneda boundary consequently has fixed trace −1. Separable base change at a trace-detecting closed point gives fixed trace −Tr(a) and positive coefficient-trace residue +Tr(a). Naturality of Cartier-twist sequences gives t_C(c∪s)=−⟨c,s⟩ for every invertible L. The fixed trace itself is defined over arbitrary fields.

Compare the raw +du Cartier extension with the normalized −du trace-one point class, and use the one-point sheaf-Ext/Grothendieck-spectral-sequence argument to identify that comparison globally on C. The positive Yoneda boundary has trace −1; separable trace base change gives t_C(δ_p(a t⁻¹dt))=−Tr(a), whereas residues give +Tr(a). The curve duality theorem then yields t_C=−t_C^res and, by naturality of the Cartier-twist connecting square, the negative fixed-trace residue pairing.

items.title: Higher-dimensional duality is not imported into the curve theorem
items.statement:
This page records three concrete curve forms of Serre duality. The statements
below retain their stated field hypotheses. Assume AC as in the cited curve
theorems, and let $C$ be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a
field $k$. All three forms use the same normalized trace
$t_C:H^1(C,\omega_C)\to k$ ([[def-smooth-projective-dualizing-line-bundle-and-trace]]).

1. For an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module $\mathcal L$ over an arbitrary field
   $k$, there is the functorial perfect pairing
   $$H^1(C,\mathcal L)\times H^0(C,\omega_C\otimes\mathcal L^{-1})\longrightarrow k,\qquad (c,s)\longmapsto t_C(c\cup s),$$
   where $\omega_C=\Omega^1_{C/k}$ ([[thm-serre-duality-curves-line-bundles]]).
   The line-bundle theorem identifies this fixed trace with the negative of
   the positive residue-sum functional under its stated perfect-field hypothesis.
2. Over an arbitrary field, for a finite locally free $\mathcal O_C$-module
   $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$, there is the functorial perfect pairing
   $$H^1(C,\mathcal E)\times H^0(C,\mathcal E^\vee\otimes\omega_C)\longrightarrow k,\qquad (c,s)\longmapsto t_C(c\cup s),$$
   using contraction and the same trace
   ([[thm-serre-duality-curves-vector-bundles]]). For rank one this is the
   line-bundle form in item 1.
3. For every coherent $\mathcal O_C$-module $\mathcal F$ over an arbitrary
   field, there are canonical, functorial isomorphisms
   $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_C}(\mathcal F,\omega_C)\cong H^1(C,\mathcal F)^*,\qquad \operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O_C}(\mathcal F,\omega_C)\cong H^0(C,\mathcal F)^*$$
   ([[thm-serre-duality-curves-coherent-sheaves]]). Both are the pairings
   formed with the fixed trace. Explicitly, the first sends
   $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\omega_C$ to the functional
   $u\mapsto t_C(H^1(\alpha)(u))$. The second sends
   $\xi\in\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathcal F,\omega_C)$ to the functional
   $s\mapsto t_C(\chi_{\omega_C}(\operatorname{Ext}^1(s,\omega_C)(\xi)))$,
   where $s:\mathcal O_C\to\mathcal F$ is a global section and
   $\chi_{\omega_C}:\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathcal O_C,\omega_C)\cong
   H^1(C,\omega_C)$ is the canonical comparison used in that theorem.

The Ext groups in item 3 are **global Ext** as defined in
[[def-sheaf-ext-for-coherent-modules]]: they are computed as the cohomology of
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_C}(\mathcal F,I^\bullet)$ for an injective
resolution of the second argument. The definition distinguishes these groups
from the sheaves $\mathcal Ext^q$ and notes that, in positive degree, global
Ext is not generally the global sections of sheaf Ext. The groups
$H^q(C,-)$ are the right-derived functors of global sections
([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]).

The coherent form is established on its own theorem page using an actual
finite locally free resolution on the curve. For an ample invertible sheaf
$L$, a sufficiently large twist $\mathcal F\otimes L^{\otimes m}$ is globally
generated; its finite-dimensional space of global sections gives a
surjection $\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal E$ finite
locally free. Its kernel $\mathcal E'$ is coherent and torsion-free, hence
finite locally free on the smooth curve. Thus the resolution used there is
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal E'\longrightarrow\mathcal E\longrightarrow\mathcal F\longrightarrow0.$$
This is the curve-specific argument in
[[thm-serre-duality-curves-coherent-sheaves]]; it does not invoke the
projective-space finite-resolution lemma.

The line-bundle and finite locally free curve theorems specialize the
published Serre duality theorem for finite locally free sheaves on a smooth
projective variety over a field
([[thm-serre-duality-smooth-projective-variety-locally-free-sheaves]]).
The coherent theorem builds on the finite locally free curve pairing and
supplies the curve-specific resolution argument above. This summary adds no
higher-dimensional duality claim. It does not import dualizing complexes,
Grothendieck duality for non-proper or higher-dimensional morphisms, local
cohomology, or relative duality over a base scheme more general than a field.

items.title: Residues on the projective line and the vanishing of their sum
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited suppliers. Let k be a perfect field and C=P^1_k with t=x_1/x_0 on U_0 and s=1/t at infinity. Every rational differential is f(t)dt. (1) For p=V(g) with g monic irreducible and u=g(t), perfectness makes g separable and g'(t) a unit; since du=g'(t)dt, if f=Σ_{n≥N}a_nu^n then res_p(fdt)=Tr_{kappa(p)/k}([u^-1](f/g')), where 1/g' is expanded as a unit series. For a simple pole c/u plus a regular term this is Tr(c/g'(bar t)); higher poles can use positive terms of the unit expansion. (2) At infinity dt=-s^-2ds, so res_infinity(fdt) is [s^-1](-f(1/s)s^-2ds); res_infinity(t^n dt) is -1 for n=-1 and 0 otherwise. (3) Monomial residues at 0 and infinity cancel; the global residue theorem gives sum_p res_p(omega)=0 for every rational differential. In particular dt/(t(t-1)) has residues -1, +1, 0 at 0, 1, infinity; its infinity expansion is -(1-s)^-1ds, with no s^-1 term. (4) The one-point tail t^-1dt represents a nonzero class in H^1(P^1,omega) because its positive residue sum is +1; H^1 is one-dimensional, and the fixed Gysin trace is -1 on this class, the negative of the positive residue sum (equal in characteristic two). [thm-global-residue-theorem-algebraic-curve; rem-duality-trace-normalization]

items.title: Serre duality on the projective line, twist by twist
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited suppliers. Let k be any field, P^1_k have coordinates x_0,x_1 and t=x_1/x_0, d≥0, and L=O(-d-2). H^1(P^1,L) and H^0(P^1,O(d)) each have dimension d+1 and the other cohomology groups of these twists vanish. For 1≤j≤d+1 let c_j=[t^-j tensor x_0^(-d-2)] be the local principal-part class at 0. For 0≤m≤d let sigma_m=t^m dt tensor x_0^(d+2) on U_0; on U_1, with s=1/t, it is -s^(d-m)ds tensor x_1^(d+2), so it is a global section corresponding to x_0^(d-m)x_1^m. The positive local coefficient at the rational origin is delta_(j,m+1). For ascending j=1,...,d+1 and m=0,...,d this is the diagonal identity; reversing the section order to m=d,...,0 displays it anti-diagonally. Over an algebraic closure, the perfect-field residue theorem gives fixed Serre pairing -delta_(j,m+1). Proper cohomology base change and compatibility of the fixed Gysin trace/cup pairing descend these entries to k, so the matrix is -I in ascending orders. It is invertible, hence the c_j form a basis by the dimension count and the pairing is perfect over every field. For d=0 the value is -1, equal to 1 in characteristic two. [lem-proper-cohomology-field-extension; lem-smooth-projective-embedding-gysin-trace-compatibility; thm-serre-duality-curves-line-bundles]

items.title: The full Riemann-Roch theorem on the projective line, in every degree
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice; it supplies Dependent Choice through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]. Let k be a field, let C = P^1_k with point at infinity, and let D be a divisor on C of degree d = deg_k(D). Every divisor on C is linearly equivalent to d[infinity] and O_C([infinity]) is isomorphic to O(1) with [O(1)] mapping to 1 under Pic(P^1_k) = Z (lem-projective-line-divisors-classified-by-degree, cor-picard-projective-line-integers), so l(D) = h^0(C, O(d)) equals d+1 for d >= 0 and 0 for d < 0 (thm-cohomology-projective-space-twisting-sheaves). The canonical divisor satisfies K_C ~ -2[infinity] and deg_k(K_C) = 2g - 2 = -2 with g = 0 (cor-canonical-degree-two-g-minus-two, lem-projective-line-divisors-classified-by-degree), so K_C - D is linearly equivalent to (-2-d)[infinity] and l(K_C - D) = h^0(C, O(-d-2)) equals 0 for d >= -1 and -d-1 for d <= -2. Subtracting, l(D) - l(K_C - D) = d + 1 in all three ranges: for d >= 0 the difference is (d+1) - 0, for d = -1 it is 0 - 0 = 0, and for d <= -2 it is 0 - (-d-1) = d+1. This verifies the full Riemann-Roch identity l(D) - l(K-D) = deg_k(D) + 1 - g (thm-full-riemann-roch-divisor) on the projective line for every integer degree, including the negative range where the index of speciality i(D) = l(K-D) = -d-1 is what makes the identity true; the special divisors are exactly those of degree at most -2, and the nonspecial divisors those of degree at least -1.

items.title: Positive-degree line bundles on a genus-one curve have exactly deg sections
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice; it supplies Dependent Choice through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve of genus one over a field k and let L be an invertible sheaf of degree n >= 1, with associated divisor D. Since n > 0 = 2g - 2, both H^1(C,L) = 0 and l(D) = h^0(C,L) = deg_k(D) + 1 - g = n (cor-h1-line-bundle-vanishes-degree-over-two-g-minus-two, cor-rr-exact-high-degree-formula, def-invertible-sheaf-of-cartier-divisor). Equivalently, with omega_C isomorphic to O_C (thm-genus-one-canonical-bundle-trivial) Serre duality reads h^1(C,L) = h^0(C, L^{-1}) = 0 because deg L^{-1} = -n < 0 (thm-serre-duality-curves-line-bundles, thm-degree-positive-line-bundle-sections-zero-bound). For n = 1 the space is one-dimensional: a degree-one invertible sheaf has a nonzero section vanishing at exactly one point, so its complete linear system is a single point of C, and every degree-one divisor is linearly equivalent to an effective degree-one divisor; the dimension formula dim |D| = deg_k(D) - g + i(D) = n - 1 recovers this and shows that the complete linear system grows by one dimension for each added degree (cor-dimension-complete-linear-system, def-little-l-divisor).

items.title: Adjunction on a smooth plane cubic: the canonical bundle is trivial
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice; it supplies Dependent Choice through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]. Let k be a field and let C = V_+(F) in P^2_k be a smooth plane cubic, that is a smooth projective plane curve of degree d = 3 (def-degree-projective-hypersurface). Adjunction gives omega_C isomorphic to O_C(d-3) = O_C (thm-adjunction-smooth-plane-curve), and the genus is g(C) = (d-1)(d-2)/2 = 1 (cor-genus-degree-smooth-plane-curve), consistent with deg_k omega_C = d(d-3) = 0 = 2g - 2 (cor-canonical-degree-two-g-minus-two). By definition omega_C = O_C(K_C) with h^0(C, omega_C) = g = 1 (cor-h0-canonical-differentials-genus), and an invertible sheaf of degree zero with a nonzero global section is trivial (cor-degree-zero-line-bundle-section-trivial); thus every canonical divisor of a plane cubic is principal, the canonical system has a single member up to scalars, and its complete canonical system has target P^0, not a positive-dimensional projective space. Conversely every genus-one curve with a rational point embeds as a plane cubic by the degree-three very ample invertible sheaf O_C(3p_0) (cor-degree-three-line-bundle-embeds-genus-one-plane-cubic), Every smooth plane cubic has genus one and trivial canonical bundle; the reverse model-existence implication requires the stated rational-point hypothesis and supplies no rational point on an arbitrary smooth plane cubic.

items.title: Adjunction on a smooth plane quartic: the canonical bundle is the hyperplane bundle
items.statement: Assume AC, as required by the cited canonical-map criterion. Let $k$ be a field and let $C=V_+(F)\subseteq\mathbb P^2_k$ be a smooth plane quartic, a smooth projective plane curve of degree $d=4$. Adjunction gives $$\omega_C\cong\mathcal O_C(d-3)=\mathcal O_C(1),$$ the restriction to $C$ of the hyperplane bundle $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^2}(1)$; the genus is $g(C)=(4-1)(4-2)/2=3$, consistently with $\deg_k\omega_C=4\cdot1=4=2g-2$. Since $h^0(C,\omega_C)=g=3$, the space of canonical sections has dimension three, so the complete canonical linear system has projective dimension two and the canonical map is a morphism to $\mathbb P^2$. That map is the given inclusion $C\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^2$: the twisted hypersurface sequence and its low-degree cohomology sequence, together with $H^0(\mathbb P^2,\mathcal O(-3))=H^1(\mathbb P^2,\mathcal O(-3))=0$, show that the restriction map $H^0(\mathbb P^2,\mathcal O(1))\to H^0(C,\mathcal O_C(1))$ is an isomorphism; hence $|K_C|=|H|$ is the linear system of lines and the canonical image of $C$ is the plane quartic itself. In particular $C$ is geometrically nonhyperelliptic, and the canonical bundle of a plane quartic is the hyperplane bundle; the canonical model of this genus-three curve is the plane quartic.

items.title: The canonical map of a hyperelliptic curve is not an embedding
items.statement: Assume AC, as required by the cited canonical-map theorem. For a smooth proper geometrically integral curve $C$ of genus $g\ge2$, geometric hyperellipticity prevents the canonical map from being a closed immersion. After extending to an algebraic closure, the canonical map factors through a degree-two map to $\mathbf P^1$ and the $(g-1)$-fold Veronese embedding. It has generic degree two onto a rational normal curve; its generic geometric fiber has two distinct points, which the canonical map identifies. This does not assert that every closed fiber has two distinct points. If the degree-two map is defined over $k$ with target $\mathbf P^1_k$, the same factorization holds over $k$.

items.title: Degree 2g-1 does not force base-point-freeness
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice; it supplies Dependent Choice through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]. Let k be a field, let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve of genus g >= 1 over k with a k-rational point p, and let K_C be a canonical divisor; put L = O_C(K_C + p), an invertible sheaf of degree deg_k(K_C + p) = 2g - 2 + 1 = 2g - 1 with associated divisor D = K_C + p (def-invertible-sheaf-of-cartier-divisor, def-canonical-line-bundle-curve, cor-canonical-degree-two-g-minus-two). Since deg_k D = 2g-1 > 2g-2 the corollary on high degrees gives l(D) = deg_k D + 1 - g = g (cor-rr-exact-high-degree-formula, thm-full-riemann-roch-divisor) and H^1(C,L) = 0 (cor-h1-line-bundle-vanishes-degree-over-two-g-minus-two). On the other hand L(-p) has the associated divisor K_C with l(K_C) = h^0(C, omega_C) = g (cor-h0-canonical-differentials-genus), so the subspace H^0(C, L(-p)) of H^0(C, L) has the same dimension g: every global section of L vanishes at p, that is, p is a base point of the complete linear system |L| (def-base-point-linear-system, def-riemann-roch-space-of-divisor). Hence the hypothesis deg >= 2g of thm-degree-two-g-line-bundle-basepoint-free cannot be weakened to deg >= 2g-1, and the bound 2g is sharp. For g = 1 the example is the classical one: L = O_C(p) has l(p) = 1 with the constant function 1 as its only section, and that section vanishes at p.

items.title: Degree 2g does not force very ampleness
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice; it supplies Dependent Choice through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]. Let k be a field, let C be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve of genus g >= 1 over k, let p be a k-rational point, let K_C be a canonical divisor, and put L = O_C(K_C + 2p), an invertible sheaf of degree deg_k(K_C + 2p) = 2g (def-invertible-sheaf-of-cartier-divisor, def-canonical-line-bundle-curve, cor-canonical-degree-two-g-minus-two). Because deg L = 2g > 2g-2 one has h^0(C,L) = 2g + 1 - g = g+1 and H^1(C,L) = 0 (cor-rr-exact-high-degree-formula, cor-h1-line-bundle-vanishes-degree-over-two-g-minus-two). For arbitrary k with the stated rational point, the degree-2g base-point-free theorem gives global generation (thm-degree-two-g-line-bundle-basepoint-free). When k is algebraically closed, the direct computation also verifies this at every closed point q: deg_k(q) = 1, so K_C + 2p - q has degree 2g-1 > 2g-2, h^0(C, L(-q)) = g = h^0(C,L) - 1, and a section of L does not vanish at q (def-base-point-linear-system). At p, however, the two vanishing conditions agree: L(-p) = O_C(K_C + p) still has degree 2g-1, so h^0(C, L(-p)) = g, while L(-2p) = O_C(K_C) has h^0(C, L(-2p)) = h^0(C, omega_C) = g (cor-h0-canonical-differentials-genus, thm-cartier-weil-divisors-curves-agree). Since a closed immersion would require the two-dimensional space of first-order jets at p to be filled, that is h^0(C,L) - h^0(C, L(-2p)) = 2, the morphism phi_L: C -> P^g_k associated with the complete linear system (thm-base-point-free-linear-system-morphism, def-complete-linear-system) has vanishing differential at p and is not a closed immersion: L is not closed H-very ample relative to Spec k (def-very-ample-invertible-sheaf-relative) although deg L = 2g. Hence the hypothesis deg >= 2g+1 of thm-degree-two-g-plus-one-line-bundle-very-ample cannot be weakened to deg >= 2g, and the bound 2g+1 is sharp; for g = 1 the example is the classical degree-two sheaf O_C(2p) on an elliptic curve, whose two sections define a double cover of P^1_k rather than an embedding.

items.title: Riemann-Hurwitz for a tame double cover with 2r branch points
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not two and let
$f:C\to\mathbb P^1_k$ be a finite surjective morphism of degree $n=2$ between
smooth proper geometrically integral curves over $k$ ([[def-algebraic-curve-over-field]])
that is tamely ramified with branch locus exactly $2r$ distinct $k$-rational
points of $\mathbb P^1_k$, the ramification index being $e_p=2$ at each of the
points $p$ of $C$ lying over the branch points. Because the residue
characteristic is not two, every residue extension of degree at most two is
separable and every ramification index that occurs is invertible, so the
tameness hypothesis is automatic here.

The fibre over a branch point $q_i$ is computed by the pullback-degree
identity $f^*[q_i]=\sum_{p}e_p[p]$: since $\deg_kf^*[q_i]=2$ and some $p$ over
$q_i$ has $e_p=2$, the branch point carries a single point $p_i$ with
$e_{p_i}=2$ and residue degree $1$, so $\kappa(p_i)=k$. Over a non-branch
point every point is unramified, and with the tame different formula
$\ell_p=e_p-1$ the different divisor is
$$R_f=\sum_{i=1}^{2r}[p_i],\qquad \deg_kR_f=2r .$$
With $g(\mathbb P^1_k)=0$ the complete Riemann-Hurwitz formula
$2g(C)-2=n(2g(\mathbb P^1_k)-2)+\deg_kR_f$
([[thm-riemann-hurwitz-complete]]) reads
$2g(C)-2=2(-2)+2r$, that is $g(C)=r-1$.

Such a cover is realized concretely by the smooth projective model $C_h$ of
$y^2=h(x)$ with $h\in k[x]$ monic and squarefree of degree $2r$ over a perfect
field $k$ of characteristic not two ([[def-perfect-field]],
[[thm-curves-function-fields-equivalence]],
[[cor-projective-embedding-every-smooth-proper-curve]]). Its two affine charts
and their overlap are constructed in Verification, step 1.4; this makes the
projection $\pi:C_h\to\mathbb P^1_k$ and the relative differential module
explicit. A point $p$ is ramified exactly when $y$ vanishes at $p$, in which
case $e_p=2$, $\kappa(p)$ is the residue field of the corresponding root, and
$\ell_p=1$. The roots of $h$ number $2r$ counted with their residue degrees,
so $\deg_kR_\pi=\deg h=2r$ and again $g(C_h)=r-1$. The infinity chart has two
$k$-rational points over $\infty$, both unramified. When $h$ splits over $k$
with distinct roots
$c_1,\dots,c_{2r}\in k$, the branch locus is exactly the $2r$ distinct
$k$-rational points $c_1,\dots,c_{2r}$ and the model is an example of the
abstract cover above.

The small cases confirm the formula: $r=1$ gives $g=0$, as for
$y^2=x^2-1$, whose smooth projective conic has a rational point and is a
projective line by [[thm-genus-zero-point-implies-projective-line]];
$r=2$ gives $g=1$, the classical Legendre family
$y^2=(x^2-1)(x^2-c)$ with $c\in k\setminus\{0,1\}$; and $r=3$ gives $g=2$, as
for a squarefree sextic. In general the genus of the model of $y^2=h(x)$ is
$r-1$.

The proof explicitly assumes the Axiom of Choice. By [F19], it supplies the
Dependent Choice required by the Cartier-to-Weil cycle argument in the divisor
suppliers; the other Choice-bearing uses are through
([[thm-curves-function-fields-equivalence]],
[[lem-degree-pullback-divisor-finite-morphism-curves]],
[[lem-curve-different-local-support-and-index-bound]],
[[lem-projective-line-divisors-classified-by-degree]],
[[thm-cartier-weil-divisors-curves-agree]],
[[thm-riemann-hurwitz-complete]], [[thm-local-ring-smooth-curve-dvr]],
[[thm-jacobian-criterion-smooth-morphism]],
[[lem-composite-finite-proper-morphism-proper]],
[[prop-modules-over-a-field-are-projective-flat-and-injective]],
[[cor-projective-embedding-every-smooth-proper-curve]], and
[[thm-genus-zero-point-implies-projective-line]]. The computations below
make no further choice.

items.title: One cocycle carried through the residue realization of Serre duality
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited suppliers. Let k be perfect, C=P^1_k with t=x_1/x_0, d≥0, and L=O(-d-2). For 1≤j≤d+1 the tail c_j=[t^-j tensor x_0^(-d-2)] at 0 is a finite-support principal part. For 0≤m≤d the dual-twist section is sigma_m=t^m dt tensor x_0^(d+2) on U_0 and -s^(d-m)ds tensor x_1^(d+2) on U_1, where s=1/t; it corresponds to x_0^(d-m)x_1^m. The positive residue pairing gives <c_j,sigma_m>=res_0(t^(m-j)dt)=delta_(j,m+1). In ascending j,m order this is diagonal identity; reversing the sections to m=d,...,0 makes it anti-diagonal. Since the sections are a basis, the invertible matrix proves that the c_j form a basis. The fixed normalized Serre matrix is the negative, with entries -delta_(j,m+1), and is perfect. For d=0 the value is -1, which equals 1 in characteristic two. [def-residue-pairing-principal-parts; thm-serre-duality-curves-line-bundles]
